title: All-temperature pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: This gives an exact free-energy formula, at every temperature, for Ising models whose coupling matrix is a Haar-random rotation of a given spectrum (for example, Hopfield/Wishart couplings G^T G). At zero temperature it gives the limiting optimum of max and min sigma^T J sigma over sign vectors, including the Gaussian ||G||_{inf->2} norm and the minimum ||sum sigma_i g_i||.
constructive: partial: a variational formula (infimum over Parisi-type paths, using the edge-extended R-transform) with no algorithm
explicit_constants: No rates. Values require numerically solving the variational problem.
opportunity: This supplies asymptotic optimal values for QUBO on rotationally invariant ensembles: Gaussian-pattern Hopfield/Wishart couplings, the random orthogonal model, and Gaussian vector balancing (min over signs of ||G sigma||). Once solved numerically, these could serve as ground-truth targets for benchmarking Ising machines, QAOA, simulated bifurcation and AMP/OAMP-type optimizers beyond SK, analogous to the Parisi value used in 281. External fields correlated with J, as in planted, CDMA or MIMO detection, are not covered.
targets: Ising-machine / QUBO benchmarking on Hopfield/Wishart instance families
AMP/OAMP/VAMP optimization theory for rotationally invariant matrices
first_step: Numerically solve the zero-temperature formula for Wishart couplings at alpha=1 and compare with simulated-annealing ground states at n≈10^3–10^4.
caveats: No outliers in the spectrum, and the deterministic external fields must have W1-convergent empirical laws. The infimum is not shown to be computable to certified precision.

title: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: Random k-SAT has a sharp limiting satisfiability threshold for every k>=3. The number of clauses at which a growing random 3-SAT formula first becomes unsatisfiable fluctuates by Theta(sqrt n). The 3-SAT threshold is a computable real number, but no efficient way to compute it is given.
constructive: partial: computability is via an unbounded certificate search with no efficiency bound. Lower certificates f_n/n - 2^67 n^{-1/6} are galactic, since they only become nontrivial for n>2^389. Upper certificates are finite rational RSB-type trials that can be evaluated exactly with interval arithmetic.
explicit_constants: Var(H_n)<=Cn with C unspecified. The lower-certificate error is 2^67 n^{-1/6}. The threshold is not evaluated (the paper does not claim 4.267).
opportunity: SAT benchmark generation: Theta(n) variance plus Wilson's lower bound gives a satisfiability window of Theta(sqrt n) clauses, a density window of order n^{-1/2}. That means finite-size-scaling exponent nu=2, contradicting the long-quoted empirical nu≈1.5 for 3-SAT. Generators of 'hard' random 3-SAT near clause/variable ratio 4.26 should expect the window to shrink as n^{-1/2}. The center's n-dependence has no rate, so per-n empirical calibration stays necessary. Secondary: finite rational upper certificates could, with certified interval evaluation of a good 1RSB-type trial, push the best rigorous upper bound below 4.4898. That project is of theory interest only.
targets: random-SAT instance generators (SAT Competition random track; CNFgen / makewff-style tools)
first_step: Measure the 10–90% satisfiability window of random 3-SAT (clauses sampled with replacement) at n=50…2000 with a CDCL solver and check sqrt(n) clause-width scaling. Then correct generator documentation that quotes nu≈1.5.
caveats: Carenini (ECCC TR26-229) has priority on threshold existence. The window is in clause count at fixed probability levels and concerns satisfiability, not solver hardness. The k=3 Theta(n) variance paper is not formalized (Lean covers O(n log n) for k=3). Computability gives no usable digits.

title: The exact factor-of-IID threshold for free Ising spins on trees
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The free Ising state on the infinite d-regular tree can be produced from independent per-vertex random labels by a symmetric rule exactly when tanh(beta) <= 1/sqrt(d-1), which is the reconstruction (Kesten–Stigum) threshold.
constructive: no: a measurable, non-finitary factor. The paper explicitly asserts no finitary coding or coding-radius bound, and no parameter-uniform or computational bound.
explicit_constants: The threshold is exact. There is no radius or complexity bound.
opportunity: No operational channel. Factors of IID are the limit objects of local randomized (distributed/GNN) algorithms on random regular graphs. Without a coding-radius bound, the result yields no bounded-round distributed sampler and no limit on GNN design. The theoretical takeaway is that correlation-decay obstructions to local sampling of the free Ising state start at the reconstruction threshold, not at uniqueness.
caveats: Infinite tree, zero field, ferromagnetic only.

title: The three-quarter exponent for honeycomb self-avoiding walk
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: A uniformly random n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice has diameter n^{3/4+o(1)}, matching Nienhuis's prediction for 2D polymers.
constructive: no
opportunity: None. The 2D Flory exponent 3/4 has long been accepted in polymer physics and is numerically confirmed to many digits. Rigour adds no new quantity.
caveats: Lean covers only supporting summability, free-energy and strip-crossing statements.

title: Optimal logarithmic mixing of the Thorp shuffle
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: The Thorp shuffle cuts the deck in half and randomly orders each pair of facing cards. It randomizes the entire order of N=2^d cards in Theta(log N) shuffles: 1600·log2 N shuffles suffice (Lean-verified), and about 2·log2 N are necessary.
constructive: yes: the shuffle is the algorithm. The result certifies a fixed-depth, oblivious random switching network, equivalently the round function of the Morris–Rogaway–Stegers small-domain cipher.
explicit_constants: Yes in the 1600d proof. Variants give 512d, 2048d and 32800d. Tracing constants: TV <= 8(1-M) + 0.5·sqrt(A^16·sum D^-3) with A=sqrt(32·C1), C1≈3.28, so TV ≈ 9e7·N^{-3/2} for large N: 3e-7 at N=2^32, 1e-21 at N=2^64. The companion bound 0.5·N^{-5} uses an unspecified absolute sweep count P.
opportunity: This is the first proof that a fixed-round (oblivious, constant-time) shuffle cipher is secure even against an adversary querying all N points, using Theta(lg N) rounds. Before, Thorp was proven only up to q < N/(4 lg N), or N^{1-1/r} queries with O(r lg N) rounds; full security in O(lg N) rounds needed the variable-time Sometimes-Recurse (SR) construction. It does not reduce rounds in practice. 1600·lg N rounds, doubled for CCA, is about 205k PRF calls per encryption at N=2^64, 100–200x more than swap-or-not/SR parameter sets of about 1000 rounds. It applies only to N=2^d, and its N^{-3/2} floor is weak exactly at FPE-sized domains (about 2^-19 at N=2^30). The reusable piece is the 'partial-permutation -> full law' Fourier transfer. It appears to turn Hoang–Morris–Rogaway's swap-or-not bound for 7N/8 fixed queries into full-permutation security with roughly 8x the rounds, qualitatively settling their full-security conjecture; that extrapolation is mine and unchecked.
targets: small-domain / format-preserving encryption research (Thorp/MRS, swap-or-not, Sometimes-Recurse: Rogaway, Hoang, Morris, Tessaro)
oblivious-shuffle / mixnet switching-network designs (Atom iterated butterfly; Czumaj O(log^2 n) networks)
first_step: Write the swap-or-not corollary: plug HMR Thm 3 at q=7N/8 into the eight-block Fourier lift (Prop orbit-lift / Thm l:main), using sign mean 0 and N divisible by 8, and tabulate concrete rounds against SR. In parallel, compute the exact TV of the Thorp shuffle for N=8 and empirical statistics for N=16–64 to estimate the true constant, which is somewhere in [2,1600].
caveats: Asymptotic in d. Powers of two only. The constant 1600 is a proof artifact, not a sharp value. The Fourier lift leaves a round-independent TV floor of about 1e8·N^{-3/2}. No deployed FPE standard uses Thorp (the Voltage-era patent US 8687802 exists). The swap-or-not transfer is an unverified extrapolation. Production oblivious shuffles (Waksman routing of a sampled permutation, bitonic sort) are already far cheaper.

title: Sharp singularity rates for symmetric random sign matrices
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
plain_english: A random symmetric matrix of ±1 entries is singular with probability (1/2+o(1))^n. With biased signs the probability is (p^2+(1-p)^2+o(1))^n, dominated by two equal rows.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: No: o(1) in the exponential base, with no rate.
opportunity: None. Numerical linear algebra and compressed sensing care about conditioning (least singular value) and real-valued ensembles, not the exact singularity probability of sign matrices, which is about 2^-n at any n where the theorem says something beyond the trivial equal-rows bound.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
subject: Topology
plain_english: Any locally compact group acting faithfully and continuously on a finite-dimensional manifold is a Lie group; in particular the p-adic integers cannot act this way.
constructive: no - structural classification theorem
opportunity: None. This is transformation-group theory. The continuous symmetry groups used in physics, robotics or vision are Lie groups by construction, so nothing downstream changes.
caveats: Long-open major conjecture with no formalization; treat as unverified claim.

title: Four-dimensional disk embedding and Wall's conjecture
subject: Topology
plain_english: In 4-dimensional topology the Freedman-Quinn disk-embedding tool fails without fundamental-group hypotheses (the free group F2 is not 'good'), and there is a 4-dimensional Poincare duality group that is not the fundamental group of any closed aspherical 4-manifold.
constructive: yes - explicit 4-manifolds/disc maps and a finitely presented group, but purely topological objects
opportunity: None. Topological 4-manifold surgery theory has no computational or engineering consumer.
caveats: Three unformalized manuscripts; resolves a central open question (F2 goodness), so high scrutiny is warranted.

title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
subject: Topology
plain_english: Two different Dehn surgeries on a nontrivial knot in the 3-sphere never give the same oriented 3-manifold.
constructive: no - non-existence theorem (Floer/gauge-theoretic style)
opportunity: None. Software that enumerates or identifies 3-manifolds (SnapPy, Regina) identifies surgeries computationally already; the theorem removes no computational step and gives no new invariant to implement.
caveats: Long-open conjecture, unformalized.

title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
subject: Topology
plain_english: Builds an explicit family of bounded-degree finite graphs (finite quotients of SL3(Z) placed over discs in the triangular lattice) on which the coarse assembly map from index theory kills a nonzero K-homology class, disproving the coarse Novikov conjecture (reduced and maximal versions).
constructive: yes - explicit graph family, but the phenomenon is asymptotic in disc radius and lives in operator K-theory/Roe algebras
explicit_constants: graph family explicit; no quantitative sizes relevant to practice
opportunity: None. Coarse assembly/Roe algebras are unrelated to topological data analysis (persistent homology does not compute coarse K-homology), and the graphs are just congruence Cayley graphs with property (T) -- no new expander construction or benchmark use beyond what Margulis/LPS graphs already give.
caveats: Reduced-assembly counterexample is Lean-formalized (CoarseAssembly); maximal version is not.

title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
subject: Topology
plain_english: Grothendieck's algebraic definition of infinity-groupoids (freely add all coherence operations via a 'coherator') reproduces exactly the homotopy theory of topological spaces, for every coherator in the Ara-Henry convention; the key step is Henry's pushout conjecture.
constructive: partial - explicit path/cylinder constructions interpreting every coherator operation, but the output is an equivalence of homotopy theories, not an algorithm
opportunity: No effect on mainstream HoTT/proof-assistant practice: Coq-HoTT, Cubical Agda and Lean already rest on simplicial/cubical/infinity-topos semantics (Kapulkin-Lumsdaine, Shulman) that interpret types as spaces. The one real formal-methods touchpoint is coherator-based type theories such as CaTT (Finster-Mimram), whose models are Grothendieck-Maltsiniotis weak omega-categories (Benjamin-Finster-Mimram): if a groupoidal CaTT/Brunerie-style coherator fits the Ara-Henry height convention, this theorem gives it a 'models = spaces' semantics. The Lean development of the elementary-expansion theorem (~12.7k lines, OAI/CategoryTheory/Globular) is a possible Mathlib contribution on globular theories.
targets: CaTT (Finster-Mimram type theory / proof assistant for weak omega-categories)
first_step: Check whether Brunerie's groupoidal coherator / the CaTT groupoid fragment satisfies Definition 'coherator convention' (generating fillers of output dimension j have arity height <= j); if so, send the semantic corollary to the CaTT developers.
caveats: Lean covers only the elementary-expansion (Henry pushout) theorem, not the semi-model structure or comparison with spaces; benefit is to type-theory semantics, not industrial verification.

title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on Riemannian spheres and closed three-manifolds

title: Yau’s nodal bounds: surfaces and higher dimensions
subject: Differential geometry

Users of eigenfunction nodal sets (spectral mesh segmentation and manifold harmonics in geometry processing, Laplacian positional encodings in geometric deep learning, Chladni/vibration analysis, quantum-chaos random-wave statistics) work with PL meshes or analytic metrics, where sqrt(k) scaling was already known (Donnelly-Fefferman) or observed; the constant is non-explicit, and the 3D-5D counterexamples require infinitely fine smooth metric tuning that no physical or discretized metric has.

title: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In a unit cube with periodic boundary conditions, the least-surface-area way to enclose a given volume fraction v (<=1/2) is a sphere for v <= 4*pi/81 (~0.155), a cylinder for v up to 1/pi (~0.318), and a flat slab beyond that -- and nothing else ever wins.
constructive: yes - exact closed-form profile and complete list of minimizers (Theorem intro:main)
explicit_constants: fully explicit: I(V)=min{(36pi)^(1/3) v^(2/3), 2 sqrt(pi v), 2}, transitions 4pi/81 and 1/pi
opportunity: Molecular simulations of liquid-vapour (or any two-phase) coexistence in cubic periodic boxes interpret finite-size effects with the capillarity approximation: the condensed phase is assumed to be a sphere, then a cylinder, then a slab, with crossovers at exactly 4pi/81 and 1/pi (Binder/MacDowell; Prestipino et al., PRE 92, 022141, 2015). Those values came from comparing only the three candidate shapes. The theorem proves that for isotropic sharp-interface energy no other morphology (perforated slabs, Schwarz/gyroid-type periodic surfaces) is ever a global minimizer, so the formulas are exact for the model. That certifies the shape assumption behind slab-geometry interfacial-tension estimates. It also confirms that triply periodic minimal-surface phases in materials (copolymer gyroid, lipid cubic phases) cannot come from interfacial area alone in a cubic cell. Some other energy term is needed.
targets: Finite-size vapour-liquid coexistence analysis in periodic boxes (Binder, MacDowell, Virnau; Prestipino et al. 2015)
Slab/direct-coexistence interfacial-tension workflows in MD/MC codes (GROMACS, LAMMPS, NIST FEASST flat-histogram MC)
Sharp-interface limits of Cahn-Hilliard / Ohta-Kawasaki (block-copolymer) models on cubic periodic cells
first_step: Write a short note or comment for the finite-size coexistence literature saying that the sphere/cylinder/slab sequence and the 4pi/81, 1/pi crossovers are now a theorem for cubic boxes (Lean-formalized). Then list the non-cubic box shapes that slab simulations actually use, as the open extension.
caveats: Applies only to the unit cubic torus. Elongated boxes, which slab simulations usually use, are not covered. Real systems add thermal fluctuations (the transitions are finite-size crossovers), Tolman/curvature corrections and anisotropic tension; copolymers add chain stretching. The transition values were already in the physics literature, and only the 'no other shapes' part is new. This is not the Kelvin/Weaire-Phelan foam-partition problem.
evidence: Web: arXiv 1509.02324 (Prestipino et al., droplet shapes in a periodic box; sph->cyl at 4pi/81, cyl->slab at 1/pi)

title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity
subject: Differential geometry

constructive: no - uniqueness theorem
opportunity: None. Mean-curvature smoothing in geometry processing (Desbrun et al., conformalized MCF) and level-set MCF in imaging/grain-growth codes operate on discretizations and viscosity solutions; tangent-flow uniqueness is a step in the theory of flow through singularities, not an algorithmic input.
caveats: Unformalized; major step in MCF singularity theory.

title: Gigli’s characterization of Alexandrov curvature
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: A metric space is an Alexandrov space with curvature >= kappa exactly when it is an RCD((n-1)kappa, n) space with Hausdorff measure whose distributional sectional curvature is >= kappa (Gigli's conjecture).
constructive: no - characterization
opportunity: None. The synthetic curvature notions used in ML (Ollivier/Forman graph Ricci curvature for over-squashing, network analysis) are discrete and not RCD; nothing here is computable from data.
caveats: Companion weak-Hessian theorem Lean-formalized; the main characterization is not.

title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In limits of manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below (noncollapsed RCD spaces), every point whose tangent cones are all Euclidean has a neighbourhood that maps to R^n with distortion at most a constant depending only on the dimension.
constructive: partial - charts built from harmonic coordinates plus a multiscale 'stretching' correction; neighbourhood size uncontrolled and L_n obtained via compactness
explicit_constants: L_n depends only on n but is not computed; chart radius not quantified
opportunity: The closest applied analogue is the theory behind eigenmap/diffusion-map manifold learning: Jones-Maggioni-Schul give local bi-Lipschitz charts from Laplacian eigenfunctions on smooth manifolds. This result extends 'bounded-distortion harmonic-type charts' to singular spaces with Ricci lower bounds, which could in principle support guarantees for data concentrated near singular sets. Without a quantitative chart scale it gives no sample-complexity or algorithmic statement.
targets: Manifold-learning theory (Laplacian eigenmaps / diffusion maps guarantees)

caveats: Not constructive from samples. ML 'curvature' on graphs is not RCD. The constant comes from a compactness argument.

title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: On any compact Riemannian manifold satisfying the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang curvature condition, the optimal-transport (squared geodesic distance) map between densities bounded above and below is a homeomorphism that is Holder continuous in both directions, with constants uniform over the density class. Injectivity domains are convex, which settles Villani's conjecture.
constructive: no - regularity theorem; Holder exponent obtained by contradiction and compactness (paper: 'no explicit exponent')
explicit_constants: none: alpha, C depend only on (M,g,lambda,Lambda) but are not computed
opportunity: The only applied use is as a regularity input for convergence or consistency proofs of OT/Monge-Ampere solvers and OT-map estimators on curved domains: OT mesh adaptation on the sphere for atmospheric models (Weller-Browne-Budd-Cullen, McRae-Cotter-Budd), finite-difference OT on the sphere (Hamfeldt-Turnquist), semi-discrete Newton methods (Kitagawa-Merigot-Thibert), and Riemannian flow matching on spheres and tori. The manifolds people actually use there were already covered: round S^n (Loeper), flat tori (Cordero-Erausquin), RP^3=SO(3) (nonfocal case, Loeper-Villani) and products of round spheres (Figalli-Kim-McCann). So the marginal applied gain is close to zero. The one possibly new case is mixed products such as S^2 x T^k.
targets: Convergence analyses of OT/Monge-Ampere solvers on the sphere (Hamfeldt-Turnquist; McRae-Cotter-Budd OT mesh adaptivity)
Riemannian flow matching / OT-map estimation on spheres and tori
Semi-discrete OT Newton solvers (Kitagawa-Merigot-Thibert) extended to manifolds
first_step: Check whether mixed products such as S^2 x T^k (nonnegative cross-curvature, hence weak MTW, by Kim-McCann) were already covered by Figalli-Kim-McCann 2013. If not, they are the only practically relevant manifolds that this result newly covers.
caveats: Covers squared Riemannian distance cost only. It does NOT cover reflector-antenna (c=-log(1-x.y) or -2log|x-y|) or freeform-lens/refractor costs, whose MTW regularity theory (Wang, Loeper 2011, Gutierrez-Huang) is separate and older. Commercial freeform design (least-squares/SQP methods) does not use these regularity theorems. The exponent is non-explicit, and the result gives no algorithm.

title: Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, rotation, and anti-de Sitter extensions

opportunity: None of engineering value. Numerical relativists sometimes use Penrose-type inequalities as sanity checks on initial data and apparent-horizon finders, but the time-symmetric (Riemannian) version already covered that use; settling the spacetime version changes no code or decision.

title: Localization and delocalization in the Anderson model
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that in the 2D Anderson model of a disordered lattice all quantum states stay localized at any disorder strength, while in 3D or higher weak disorder leaves an energy band of extended (conducting) states.
constructive: no: spectral-type statements
opportunity: This rigorously confirms the long-standing physics consensus from scaling theory (Simon's Problem 1). It does not change how disordered photonic, acoustic or electronic devices are modelled or simulated.

title: Sharp finite-matrix Lieb–Thirring inequalities and all equality cases
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Determines the exact best constant in the 1D Lieb-Thirring inequality, which bounds the sum of powers of bound-state energies of a Schrodinger operator, for exponents between 1/2 and 3/2. It covers matrix-valued potentials and classifies when equality holds.
constructive: yes for extremizers (explicit sech^2 solitons)

The paper notes that the gamma=1 operator-valued case was already obtained by Read-Schulz 2026, so no improvement to 3D DFT kinetic bounds follows from the new range.
caveats: Finite matrices only; gamma=1 case not new.

title: The ionization and generalized ionization conjectures
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that a molecule with M nuclei and total nuclear charge Z can bind at most Z + C*M electrons for a universal constant C. Neutral-atom first ionization energies and outer radii are bounded above and below by universal constants, and multi-electron ionization energies follow Thomas-Fermi asymptotics.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: C universal but not numerically specified; TF coefficient and (81 pi^2/2)^{1/3} radius constant explicit
opportunity: This is a landmark mathematical-physics result with no engineering channel. Chemists already know from experiment and computation that atoms bind at most about Z+1 or Z+2 electrons. A non-explicit universal C cannot inform basis-set design, DFT functionals, or ionization-energy predictions.
caveats: Nonrelativistic; constant not effective.

title: Strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Shows that for generic small perturbations of a rotating (Kerr) black-hole spacetime, the interior cannot be extended past its natural boundary even in a weak sense. This is a local version of strong cosmic censorship.
constructive: no (genericity/Baire argument)
opportunity: Pure general relativity; no applied channel.

title: Area laws and tensor networks for two-dimensional gapped systems
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that the unique ground state of any gapped local Hamiltonian on a 2D square-lattice region has entanglement bounded by its boundary length (an area law). On LxL grids such a state can be written as a PEPS tensor network with polynomial bond dimension and 1/L error, but only as an existence statement.
constructive: no: explicitly an existence theorem; tensors may depend arbitrarily on the ground state, and no efficient construction or contraction is claimed
explicit_constants: no: bond dimension C*L^c with C,c depending on (q,J,Delta) only through compactness-style choices; internal error powers like L^-60 and patch ranks e^{C_Q(1+u)} indicate a very large exponent c
opportunity: This settles the 2D area law and the global-vector PEPS conjecture (Cirac-Garre-Rubio-Perez-Garcia Questions 7-8) for open square grids, which is a big result in quantum information theory. It does not by itself yield an efficient classical algorithm for 2D gapped ground states. The proof prepares the target vector as a free resource, gives no handle on finding the tensors, and general PEPS contraction is #P-hard. A 2D analogue of the Landau-Vazirani-Vidick 1D algorithm would need further research. The useful ingredients are the collar estimates and the positive operators with decaying tails that annihilate the ground state, which may support approximate-ground-state-projector (AGSP) style constructions. For tensor-network practitioners it only justifies, after the fact, an ansatz they already trust; the exponent gives no guidance on bond dimension.
targets: PEPS / 2D tensor-network community (ITensor, TeNPy, quimb, peps-torch)

caveats: Not Lean-formalized; very long unrefereed proofs; open boundary only (torus translation-invariant formulation not covered); existence only.

title: Exactly three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that at most 3 mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension 6, so the complete set of 7 that exists in prime-power dimensions is impossible for d=6. The upper bound is a large floating-point computer search with certified rounding.

Optimal (d+1)-basis tomography and full-MUB QKD protocols do not exist for a qubit-qutrit (d=6) system, so practitioners must use SIC-POVMs, overcomplete or product measurements, or other dimensions. Practice already assumed this after numerical evidence from 2007 onward, so the value is mainly certification and updating open-problem lists, textbooks and protocol surveys.

IQOQI/Kruger-Werner open quantum problems list (MUB entry)
Bengtsson-Zyczkowski 'Geometry of Quantum States' and MUB surveys (McNulty-Weigert)
