title: Positive-temperature Bose–Einstein condensation and exact quantum depletion
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves Bose-Einstein condensation at positive temperature for the dilute hard-sphere Bose gas. It also proves Bogoliubov's formula for the fraction of particles kicked out of the condensate at zero temperature, 8/(3 sqrt(pi)) sqrt(rho a^3).
constructive: no
explicit_constants: depletion constant 8/(3 sqrt pi) explicit; temperature/density thresholds existential
opportunity: This rigorously confirms textbook Bogoliubov theory, which cold-atom experiments (for example uniform-trap depletion measurements) already use. No experimental or computational practice changes.

title: The spin-one Haldane gap
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves the Haldane conjecture for the spin-1 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain on even rings: the energy gap above the ground state stays bounded away from zero as the chain grows, with an explicit lower bound.
constructive: yes: computer-assisted with exact rational/interval data in verification/
explicit_constants: yes: gap > log(20)/784 ~ 0.0038 for even L>=2304 and > (4/105)log(80/79) ~ 0.00048 for L>=60, against the DMRG value 0.4105
opportunity: We considered and rejected the MBQC channel. Symmetry-protected Haldane-phase states are known computational wires (Else-Schwarz-Bartlett-Doherty). The companion boundary-field paper plus Tasaki's index theorem now rigorously place the Heisenberg point in that phase. However, phase membership was already established numerically by White-Huse 1993, practical MBQC uses AKLT or cluster states, and the proven gap bound is about 100x below the true gap. Nothing changes in practice.
caveats: Not Lean-formalized; bound far from sharp.

title: Uniform Laughlin gap and stability under bounded scalar disorder
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that the standard model Hamiltonian for the 1/3 fractional quantum Hall (Laughlin) state on a sphere has an energy gap bounded below uniformly in particle number. The gap survives weak bounded disorder.
constructive: partial: sum-of-squares certificate with integer data (verification/rows.txt); flux threshold not explicit
explicit_constants: gap >= 1/25 for sufficiently large systems (threshold not explicit); disorder threshold existential
opportunity: We considered and rejected the topological-QC channel. Laughlin anyons are abelian and not universal for topological quantum computation, and the V1 pseudopotential gap is an idealization already characterized numerically (Haldane-Rezayi). Proving it rigorously does not change adiabatic state preparation on quantum simulators or FQH device modelling.
caveats: Sphere geometry, V1 only, non-explicit system-size threshold.

title: Threshold and positive-energy bound states of the BFSS matrix model
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that the BFSS matrix model of M-theory has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every N. For SU(2) it also has infinitely many positive-energy bound states, contradicting a claim in the original BFSS paper.
constructive: no
opportunity: High-energy theory only. Lattice and Monte Carlo BFSS simulation groups might note the positive-energy bound states, but this is not an applied channel.

title: Bloch's law, its lattice correction, and the spherical magnetization law
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves Bloch's T^(3/2) law for how magnetization of a 3D quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet drops at low temperature, with the exact coefficient and the first lattice correction. It also proves that spontaneous magnetization exists in dimension 3 and above.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: yes: leading coefficient and correction 3 zeta(5/2)(beta S)^{-5/2}/(128 pi^{3/2})
opportunity: This rigorously confirms spin-wave theory (Bloch, Dyson) that magnetometry fits already use. Nothing changes in practice.

title: Entanglement without distillable secret key
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Builds an explicit entangled two-party state on C^10 x C^10 from which no secret key can be distilled, even with unlimited two-way public discussion. This answers the 2005 open problem 'secret key from all entangled states?' negatively. It also gives an explicit PPT channel whose square is not entanglement breaking, disproving the PPT-squared conjecture.
constructive: yes: explicit integer matrices define the maps and state; exact-arithmetic verification scripts included
explicit_constants: yes: explicit 10x10 state; trace-distance gap >= 1/10 from an ideal key bit for every protocol length
opportunity: For QKD theory, entanglement is necessary but now provably not sufficient for key, even with two-way post-processing. The PPT-squared disproof reopens questions about key repeaters and PPT links in quantum networks, where limitation results (Bauml-Christandl-Horodecki-Winter) leaned on related structure. Deployed QKD already computes key rates numerically per protocol, so nothing changes in fielded systems. The explicit 10x10 state could serve as a test case for entanglement-detection and key-rate tools.
targets: QKD security theory (private states, key repeaters)
first_step: Check which quantum-key-repeater no-go results assumed PPT-squared, and whether the M_21 channel Theta gives a two-link chain with positive repeated key.
caveats: Zero-key result holds within the paper's 'admitted completed protocol' model. Lean covers the PPT-composition counterexamples, not the secrecy theorem.

title: The entropy photon-number inequality
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves the entropy photon-number inequality, the quantum-optics analogue of Shannon's entropy power inequality for beam-splitter mixing. Thermal light is the worst case at fixed entropy. Consequences include the exact minimum output entropy of multimode thermal attenuators with entangled inputs and the exact capacity region of the degraded two-receiver pure-loss bosonic broadcast channel.
constructive: yes for consequences: optimal inputs are thermal / coherent-state superposition codes; region given in closed form
explicit_constants: yes: closed-form capacity region R_B<=g(eta_B beta N), R_C<=g(eta_C N)-g(eta_C beta N)
opportunity: Closes a 2007 conjecture (Guha-Erkmen-Shapiro) on which a family of optical-communication capacity theorems were conditional. The paper itself makes the pure-loss broadcast region unconditional. Other results with converses that needed the multimode constrained minimum-output-entropy statement may also become unconditional, notably the bosonic wiretap capacity (Guha-Shapiro-Erkmen 2008) and the pure-loss trade-off capacities (Wilde-Hayden-Guha 2012); the paper explicitly does not claim these, so each must be checked. The beneficiaries are quantum optical communication theory (fiber, free-space, satellite links) and the textbooks that state these as conditional.
targets: textbooks: Holevo 'Quantum Systems, Channels, Information', Serafini 'Quantum Continuous Variables', Wilde 'Quantum Information Theory'
first_step: Deep-dive: list every published bosonic capacity theorem marked 'conditional on EPnI / minimum-output-entropy conjecture 2'. For each, check whether Cor. thermal-attenuator (identical thermal attenuators with entangled multimode inputs, including N_B=0) is exactly the missing converse ingredient.
caveats: Finite-energy, finite-mode, identical attenuators only; the paper disclaims amplifier, wiretap, noisy-broadcast and quantum-capacity statements. Practical optical links operate far from Holevo limits, so the value is in theory and guarantees.

title: Parity is not in QAC<sup>0</sup>
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that constant-depth quantum circuits built from one-qubit gates and many-qubit Toffoli gates cannot compute the parity of n bits, even with polynomially many helper qubits. Consequences include obstructions to constant-depth fanout, majority, and preparation of cat-like (GHZ/Dicke) states in that gate model.
constructive: no: lower bound
explicit_constants: asymptotic only (holds for all sufficiently large n at fixed depth; threshold not explicit)
opportunity: Settles an architecture question. Native multi-controlled-Z gates, of the kind Rydberg-blockade neutral-atom platforms offer, are provably not a substitute for fanout: without mid-circuit measurement plus feedforward, or a fanout-type global gate such as ion-trap global Molmer-Sorensen, parity and GHZ-type states cannot be produced in constant depth. This supports the dynamic-circuit route (constant-depth GHZ with measurement and feedforward) for compiler resource estimates and architecture comparisons.
targets: neutral-atom compilation (QuEra Bloqade, Pasqal Pulser) native C^kZ gates
Qiskit/tket depth and resource estimation docs
first_step: Write a short note mapping the theorem and its fanout/Dicke corollaries onto native gate sets (C^kZ versus global MS) for architecture-comparison papers.
caveats: Asymptotic; says nothing at n~100 with unspecified thresholds. Excludes measurement and feedforward; QAC0 with fanout gates remains powerful.

title: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that estimating the ground-state energy of electrons around fixed nuclei in full 3D continuum space is QMA-hard, the quantum analogue of NP-hard, even when every nucleus is a proton. The hard instances are carefully spaced hydrogen-nucleus clusters that emulate a hard spin model.
constructive: yes: deterministic poly-time reduction outputs nuclear positions and thresholds
explicit_constants: polynomial but unspecified scales (k=ceil(C n^A), lambda=8k^3/rho with 'sufficiently large absolute' A,C)
opportunity: Removes the 'finite orbital basis' loophole in O'Gorman et al. 2022. Worst-case ab initio electronic structure, even with hydrogen only and full continuum minimization, has no efficient general algorithm on classical or quantum computers unless QMA collapses. This supports skeptical framing of claims of exponential quantum advantage in chemistry (it must come from structure, not generality). Practical quantum-chemistry codes are unaffected because real molecules are not these polynomially stretched gadget clusters.
first_step: Cite in quantum-advantage and complexity-of-chemistry discussions as the continuum and unit-charge version of the electronic-structure QMA-hardness result.
caveats: Hardness only; QMA membership not asserted. Instances are galactic (polynomially stretched H clusters at unspecified large powers). Consensus already expected this.

title: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Computes exactly how many classical bits per use can be sent through a qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel, the standard model of energy relaxation at finite temperature. The answer is a one-variable maximization, and entangled inputs across channel uses do not help.
constructive: yes: explicit formula and explicit optimal binary pure-state ensemble
explicit_constants: yes: C = (1/ln2) max_p { h((1-gamma)p+gamma nu) - g(gamma nu(1-nu)+gamma(1-gamma)(p-nu)^2) }
opportunity: Settles an open problem flagged by Leditzky-Kaur-Datta-Wilde 2018. For thermal-relaxation noise, product (non-entangled) binary signalling achieves capacity, so code designers need not search over entangled input codewords; collective decoding is still required. It also yields additivity with any finite-dimensional partner channel. The formula can replace the upper and lower bounds (Khatri-Sharma-Wilde 2020, Fang 2026) in capacity tables.
targets: Khatri-Wilde 'Principles of Quantum Communication Theory' / Khatri-Sharma-Wilde 2020 bounds
quantum Shannon theory textbooks and capacity tables
noise-model-aware capacity studies of superconducting-qubit links (thermal_relaxation-type noise)
first_step: Implement the one-line capacity function, reproduce the Khatri-Sharma-Wilde figure with the exact curve, and post a note or erratum to bound-table maintainers.
caveats: Unassisted classical capacity only; quantum and private capacities are not addressed.

title: Threshold repetition for entangled games
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that for any two-player game played with quantum entanglement, the chance of winning well above the best single-game rate across k parallel repetitions decays exponentially in k. This lets such games be amplified to near-certain accept/reject.
constructive: partial: bound is explicit for fixed question distributions
explicit_constants: universal rate kappa0*delta^5/(1+log d) with kappa0=1/(16(4B4)^4), B4 non-explicit (Song's lemma); explicit cubic rate delta^3/(16384(1+kappa_mu)(1+log d))
opportunity: In principle this underpins parallel (one-shot) device-independent protocols, since threshold soundness is exactly what parallel DIQKD and randomness protocols need. In practice the explicit rate is galactic. For CHSH (kappa_mu=96, d=4) the cubic rate at delta=0.1 is about 2.6e-10 per round, so about 1e11 rounds are needed for 1e-10 soundness, against roughly 1e6-1e8 rounds in DIQKD experiments. Winning-probability concentration is also not a key-rate or min-entropy bound; entropy-accumulation (EAT) proofs remain the tool of choice.
targets: parallel DIQKD / DI randomness theory (Jain-Miller-Shi; Vidick)
caveats: Finite-dimensional strategies only. Lean formalizes only the weaker delta^13 rate. The delta^5 rate rests on an external lemma (Song 2026).

title: Failure of Kohn–Sham ensemble representation
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Constructs a three-electron, two-nucleus Coulomb system whose true ground-state electron density cannot be reproduced by any ensemble of non-interacting electrons in one ordinary local potential. That is the existence assumption behind exact Kohn-Sham DFT. It also shows that the exchange-correlation potential has no local first-variation representative at that density.
constructive: partial: explicit Hamiltonian form, but nuclear charge Z is specified only by a nonnumerical formula with D=10^200
explicit_constants: no effective numerical bound on Z; separation (2D/Z) with D=10^200
opportunity: Gives analytic backing to numerically observed failures of Kohn-Sham density inversion (Trushin-Erhard-Gorling 2024; Erhard-Trushin-Gorling 2025). The mechanism, a nodal plane in the leading ionization amplitude that produces anomalous density decay (Gori-Giorgi-Gal-Baerends), is generic to open-shell systems, even though the certified instance is unphysical. Developers of exact-xc-potential inversion tools and ensemble DFT should treat non-convergence near nodal-plane asymptotics as possibly genuine and prefer regularized formulations (Moreau-Yosida / Kvaal-Ekstrom-Teale-Helgaker).
targets: density-inversion codes (n2v, KS-pies; Wu-Yang/ZMP inversions in PySCF-based workflows)
first_step: Deep-dive: compare the paper's plane-obstruction hypotheses (Thm. obstruction) with the open-shell atoms where TEG24 saw inversion failures, and decide whether the obstruction plausibly applies to real systems.
caveats: Potential class L^{3/2}+L^infty only (distributional potentials not excluded). Instance is galactic and its charge nonnumerical. Not Lean-formalized; single manuscript.

title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Gives a polynomial-size quantum circuit family over a fixed finite gate set that factors every integer with probability exactly one, rather than with high probability.
constructive: yes
explicit_constants: polynomial but large; the paper says its 'large polynomial parameters are not intended as practical resource improvements'
opportunity: None for compilers or cryptographic resource estimates. Shor plus verification and retry is already Las Vegas with tiny failure probability, hardware noise dominates any gain from exactness, and the construction is costlier than Gidney-Ekera style circuits. It matters only for exact-quantum-complexity theory.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Shows that every well-behaved (unitary, strongly rational) vertex operator algebra yields a conformal net with the same braided representation category. This links two mathematical frameworks for 2D conformal field theory.
constructive: no
opportunity: Pure mathematical physics. The tie to unitary modular tensor categories (anyon models) is too remote to affect topological-QC engineering.

title: QAOA attains the SK optimum in the thermodynamic-first limit
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Proves that QAOA, a near-term quantum optimization heuristic, can get arbitrarily close to the optimal energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass at some fixed depth, in the infinite-size limit. It gives no bound on that depth and no way to find the angles.
constructive: no: existence of depth and angles; the paper says it gives 'no quantitative finite-size estimate, depth bound, or efficient procedure for choosing the angles'
opportunity: Practically this is a statement of no advantage. Montanari's classical message-passing algorithm already reaches (1-eps) of the SK optimum in polynomial time once the zero-temperature Parisi measure has full support, and the companion paper (independently of Chen 2026) proves that full support, making the classical algorithm unconditional. QAOA-on-SK benchmarks (Basso et al.; Google 2021 experiment) get no angle schedule or depth estimate.
targets: QAOA benchmark literature (SK / MaxCut on large-degree regular graphs)
caveats: Thermodynamic limit first; Lean covers only the Parisi-variational identities and full support, not QAOA convergence.

title: From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Under strong axiomatic assumptions, proves that a 4D quantum field theory with scale symmetry also has local conformal symmetry.
constructive: no
opportunity: Pure QFT foundations; no applied channel.
caveats: Heavy hypotheses; local (not global) conformal conclusion.

title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Shows that a fixed polynomial-size quantum circuit with access to a suitably chosen classical oracle can approximately implement any n-qubit unitary, with diamond-norm error 1/2.
constructive: no for the oracle: the target-dependent Boolean oracle may have an exponential truth table, and no efficient classical construction is given
opportunity: None for quantum compilers (Qiskit UnitarySynthesis, tket, BQSKit). Computing the oracle is the whole difficulty and is not addressed, and error 1/2 is useless for compilation. This is a quantum-complexity result about the Aaronson-Kuperberg problem.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: The optimal quartic separation between randomized and quantum queries
subject: Mathematical physics
plain_english: Constructs Boolean functions where randomized algorithms need about the fourth power of the number of queries quantum algorithms need, so the known quartic upper bound is tight.
constructive: yes (explicit function family)
opportunity: Query-complexity theory. It caps the polynomial quantum speedups possible for total functions, but no practical algorithm or decision depends on whether the cap is cubic or quartic.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that the 3D relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell equations for a collisionless plasma of one particle species have a unique smooth solution for all time from any smooth initial data, with no size or symmetry restrictions.
constructive: no: global regularity
explicit_constants: none stated; momentum-support bound may grow with T and is not quantified in the theorem
opportunity: A priori error analyses of Vlasov-Maxwell solvers (PIC convergence proofs, DG and semi-Lagrangian error estimates) assume a smooth solution exists on [0,T]. For the one-species relativistic model that assumption is now a theorem, so such convergence results can be stated unconditionally. Production plasma codes are unaffected, and real plasmas are multi-species.
targets: context: WarpX, OSIRIS, EPOCH, VPIC (no code change)
caveats: One species only; no quantitative growth bounds; whole-space, compact support.

title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Builds rough initial gas data on a periodic box from which the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation has two different weak solutions, both conserving mass, momentum and energy locally.
constructive: partial: construction via concentrating cold jets at geometrically shrinking scales
opportunity: None. The nonuniqueness needs singular, unbounded-amplitude data at shrinking scales. DSMC and deterministic Boltzmann solvers (SPARTA, DSMC codes, discrete-velocity methods) work with bounded data, where uniqueness theory (Kaniel-Shinbrot, Ukai, Duan et al.) applies.

title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Derives the Boltzmann equation from Newtonian particle dynamics for realistic short-range potentials, including attractive wells, over the whole time interval where the kinetic solution stays regular. A companion proves that fluctuations follow the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: convergence rates of form eps^c with unspecified c
opportunity: This is a foundations-of-kinetic-theory result. It could be cited to justify fluctuating-Boltzmann noise models used in fluctuating DSMC and fluctuating hydrodynamics, but those communities already validate their models empirically and through Wagner-type DSMC convergence theorems. No action follows.
caveats: Regular kinetic interval only; hard spheres for fluctuations.

title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Shows that electrical (Dirichlet-to-Neumann) measurements on any small patch of the boundary, with currents injected and voltages read on that same patch, determine a smooth anisotropic conductivity up to coordinate change, and a smooth scalar conductivity uniquely, in 3D and above. Conversely, two different rough (merely bounded) 3D conductivities can give identical full-boundary measurements.
constructive: no for uniqueness (no reconstruction or stability); nonuniqueness pair built from an infinite nested hierarchy of scalar blocks
explicit_constants: none (contrast C/c unspecified; no stability modulus)
opportunity: Partial-data electrical impedance and resistivity tomography is the realistic setting: chest-belt EIT, and geophysical ERT with surface electrodes only. Same-patch uniqueness for smooth conductivities in 3D is the theoretical green light for those reconstructions. The rough-conductivity counterexample shows that regularity priors are mathematically necessary, not just convenient. It may also interest DC and thermal metamaterial 'illusion' design, as exact indistinguishable isotropic bounded conductivities, but the construction uses infinitely many nested scales. Neither result supplies stability estimates or algorithms, and EIT is only logarithmically stable.
targets: EIT/ERT reconstruction (EIDORS, pyGIMLi, ResIPy, SimPEG DC resistivity)
caveats: Uniqueness only. Lean formalizes the nonuniqueness pair only. Patch results are long and unformalized.

title: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture and local weak-L4 gradient bounds
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that in the classic Mumford-Shah image-segmentation model, every optimal edge set in 2D is locally a smooth curve, a curve ending at a crack tip, or three curves meeting at 120 degrees, with finitely many pieces in any compact region.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: Holder exponent alpha and weak-L4 constants not explicit
opportunity: This justifies structural assumptions (edges as finitely many regular arcs, triple junctions, crack tips) in curve-based Mumford-Shah segmentation and in 2D variational brittle fracture (Francfort-Marigo / Ambrosio-Tortorelli phase-field fracture). Practice already assumes this structure, and modern segmentation is mostly learned, so there is no operational change.
caveats: Interior only; bounded fidelity data; not formalized.

title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Shows that 7 is the first dimension where minimizers of the one-phase Bernoulli free-boundary problem can have singular points, so free boundaries are smooth up to dimension 6.
constructive: partial: explicit 7D singular cone
opportunity: Free-boundary and shape-optimization applications live in dimensions 2-3, where regularity was already known. No applied change.

title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that any finite-energy invertible deformation of a 3D body (a Sobolev homeomorphism) can be approximated arbitrarily well, in energy norm, by smooth invertible deformations onto the same target. The route passes through piecewise-linear invertible maps.
constructive: partial: staged construction (locally bi-Lipschitz, then PL homeomorphism, then smoothing) built on Moise-Bing PL topology; not algorithmic
opportunity: The paper's intermediate step (Prop. sm:bilip-pl) means injective piecewise-affine maps on tetrahedral meshes are W^{1,p}-dense among 3D Sobolev homeomorphisms. That is a density statement relevant to injectivity-constrained P1 finite elements in nonlinear elasticity and to foldover-free volumetric mapping in geometry processing. It does not give energy convergence for elastic energies with determinant blow-up (the paper says so), so the Lavrentiev-gap question in FEM remains open.
caveats: Locally finite (not finite) PL meshes; no rates; no energy convergence.

title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that on any smooth simply connected planar region, the second Neumann eigenfunction (the 'hot spots' mode) has no interior critical points, so its hottest and coldest points lie on the boundary.
constructive: no
opportunity: We considered and rejected the shape-analysis channel. Graphics and shape-analysis pipelines already use Fiedler-vector extrema as heuristic boundary or diameter endpoints, and the graph version of hot spots can fail, so this continuum theorem changes nothing in practice.

title: The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves the Lane-Emden and Henon-Lane-Emden conjectures: certain coupled nonlinear elliptic PDE systems have no positive solutions on all of space in the subcritical range.
constructive: no
opportunity: This is a Liouville theorem used inside PDE a-priori-bound arguments. It is unrelated to the astrophysical Lane-Emden ODE used in stellar modelling.

title: Stable blowup for the defocusing Schrödinger equation
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: For a very high-power defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the 12-dimensional torus, finds an open set of smooth initial data whose solutions blow up in finite time.
constructive: partial
opportunity: Optical and BEC NLS models are 1-3D with cubic or quintic nonlinearity. Dimension 12 with huge powers has no physical or numerical relevance.

title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that static boundary measurements on a 3D elastic body (displacements in, tractions out, over the whole surface) uniquely determine both spatially varying Lame elastic moduli, for any smooth coefficients.
constructive: no: uniqueness only, no reconstruction or stability
opportunity: This settles the elastic Calderon uniqueness problem that underlies boundary-data elastic imaging and non-destructive testing. Clinical elastography (MRE, shear-wave ultrasound) uses interior and dynamic data, which is a different and easier inverse problem, so the practical effect is limited to theoretical justification of static boundary-only modalities.
targets: context: MRE and shear-wave elastography (different data, no change)
caveats: Full boundary data; smooth coefficients; no stability.

title: Nonattainment of the three-marginal Coulomb Monge problem
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Constructs a smooth electron density for which the optimal 'strictly correlated electrons' arrangement of three electrons cannot be described by co-motion maps (positions of electrons 2 and 3 as functions of electron 1). The optimal energy can still be approached by such maps.
constructive: yes: explicit mechanism (five small components, two families of optimal triples, 1/3 vs 1/6 mass imbalance) but neighborhoods chosen 'sufficiently small' via local calculus
explicit_constants: no numerical radii; inverse-power Riesz extension for all d>=2, s>0
opportunity: Settles a design question for strictly-correlated-electron (SCE) DFT numerics. For N>=3 in 3D, solvers cannot assume the Monge or co-motion ansatz in general. Kantorovich-plan methods (multi-marginal Sinkhorn, Friesecke et al. GenCol) are the safe default, while map-parametrized solvers still give correct energies only in the infimum. A discretized version of the construction would make a good test instance: a correct multi-marginal OT solver must return the split two-branch plan.
targets: SCE / multi-marginal OT DFT numerics (Gori-Giorgi, Friesecke, Nenna groups)
GenCol column generation for Coulomb MMOT
first_step: Instantiate the five-ball density numerically and run GenCol and multi-marginal Sinkhorn to check that both recover the non-Monge (branch-splitting) optimal plan.
caveats: No external potential or ground-state realization (density is artificial). SCE energy and potential are unaffected since the infima agree.

title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that the optimal-transport (Brenier) map from a uniform distribution on a convex body to any target distribution varies with the target with Holder exponent 1/3 in the 2-Wasserstein distance. One constant works for all targets, including atomic ones, and three-atom examples show 1/3 cannot be improved.
constructive: yes for constants: explicit C* = sqrt(12 d R^2 (1+sqrt162)^2 + 28 L^2 P_K/|K|); sharpness by explicit three-atom family
explicit_constants: yes, but large: C*~96 for unit square to unit square, so the bound beats the trivial diam(Y) bound only when W2 < ~3e-6
opportunity: Gives the sharp worst-case guarantee for linearized-OT (LOT) embeddings and plug-in or semi-discrete Monge-map estimators with a uniform reference. Map error is at most C W2^{1/3}, so a plug-in estimator from n samples has worst-case rate about n^{-1/(3d)} with no target regularity, and no estimator analysis can beat exponent 1/3 without extra assumptions. This improves the W1^{1/6} bound of Delalande-Merigot 2023 and refutes Letrouit's conjectured square-root bound. Useful for guarantee statements; the numerical constant is too large to certify anything at practical scales.
first_step: Update the LOT and Monge-estimator stability statements (docs and survey tables) to the sharp W2^{1/3} uniform exponent, citing the three-atom sharpness family.
caveats: Uniform source on a convex body only. Fully Lean-formalized (bound and sharpness).

title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension 8: monotone entire solutions of the Allen-Cahn equation depend on only one direction.
constructive: no
opportunity: Phase-field (Allen-Cahn) simulations do not depend on classifying entire solutions in R^8.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Constructs smooth external forcings for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations, starting from fluid at rest, such that a marked fluid particle enters a target region exactly when a given Turing machine halts. This makes particle-reachability under designed forcing undecidable.
constructive: yes: a terminating compiler from Turing machine to force program
explicit_constants: effective but encodes the tape in exact real coordinates
opportunity: No CFD implication. The construction stores unbounded information in exact real coordinates (the paper says it is not a bound on finite-precision recovery). Any finite-time, finite-precision simulation question remains decidable, and the forcing is adversarially designed, not physical. It does not show turbulence or CFD verification is undecidable.
caveats: Box-transport paper repaired on Oct 7 2026 (torus-projection and common-clock estimates).

title: Interior $`C^{1,\alpha}`$ regularity for infinity-harmonic functions
subject: Partial differential equations
plain_english: Proves that infinity-harmonic functions, the 'best Lipschitz extensions' of boundary data, are continuously differentiable with a Holder-continuous gradient in every dimension 3 and above.
constructive: no: exponent from compactness
opportunity: The infinity-Laplacian underlies AMLE image interpolation (Caselles-Morel-Sbert) and graph-based Lipschitz learning (Kyng-Rao-Sachdeva-Spielman; Calder). Continuum C^{1,alpha} regularity is the kind of input consistency and convergence-rate proofs for those schemes need, but the non-explicit exponent gives no usable rate.
caveats: Interior only; not formalized.

title: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: The paper builds exotic finitely generated groups that disprove two central conjectures linking a group's geometry to the K-theory of its operator algebra. Reduced Baum–Connes assembly fails rational injectivity (torsion-free example) and fails surjectivity (a projection of irrational trace). A torsion-free group is also given whose reduced C*-algebra contains a projection other than 0 and 1, refuting Kadison–Kaplansky.
constructive: partial: the groups are explicit geometric/small-cancellation constructions, but nothing about them is algorithmic
explicit_constants: 0<tau(e)<1/2; geometric constants C_*, C_bullet and 'sufficiently large ell' are left unspecified
opportunity: None. PHYS was checked and rejected. K-theory of group and crossed-product C*-algebras is used for gap labelling and the classification of topological phases (periodic and aperiodic materials). Those symmetry groups are Z^d or amenable, and for amenable groups Baum–Connes is a theorem (Higson–Kasparov). The counterexample groups are exotic non-amenable constructions that no material model encounters.
caveats: Three unformalized manuscripts that overturn decades-old conjectures. These are extraordinary claims with no Lean coverage.

title: Rigidity and arithmetic of lattice von Neumann algebras
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: For group von Neumann algebras of lattices in Lie groups over local fields with property (T), possibly twisted by a 2-cocycle, every finite-index bimodule into any other ICC group factor comes from an actual finite-index subgroup isomorphism. The group and cocycle can therefore be recovered from the algebra.
constructive: no: these are classification and rigidity theorems
explicit_constants: n/a (a normalizing constant c_0 appears in an isometry)
opportunity: None. This is W*-rigidity and superrigidity theory for property (T) lattices, with no computational or physical use.
caveats: Not Lean-formalized.

title: Isomorphism of the free group factors
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: The von Neumann algebras generated by free groups with 2 and with 3 generators are isomorphic. By the classical dichotomy, all interpolated free group factors are then isomorphic.
constructive: partial: an iterative construction (polynomial flows plus small-cocycle estimates) produces a free Haar n-tuple inside L(F_{n+1}). It is a limiting argument, not an algorithm.
opportunity: None. Free probability does have applied uses: asymptotic freeness in random-matrix models for MIMO capacity and deep-network Jacobian spectra. Those calculations use free convolution of distributions and never depend on whether L(F_2) and L(F_3) are isomorphic.
caveats: Headline result is Lean-formalized; the claim is extraordinary.

title: Kadison's similarity conjecture
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Every bounded unital homomorphism from a C*-algebra into Hilbert-space operators can be turned into a *-homomorphism by conjugating with one bounded invertible operator. A byproduct is a single universal hyperreflexivity constant for all von Neumann algebras.
constructive: no: S exists, but no bound on its condition number is given
explicit_constants: Traceable but enormous: c_row=4*sqrt2, c0=(1+4c_row)^2, c1=6pi^2(1+4c0), C=3*max(3c1+2,...)+2 ~ 1.2e6. The hyperreflexivity constant is <= 2C ~ 2.4e6.
opportunity: None. QUANT was checked and rejected. Quantum information uses 'approximately commuting implies close to the commutant' and stability of near-representations, but only for finite-dimensional, hence injective, algebras. There Christensen-type distance and similarity bounds with small constants have been known since the 1970s-80s. The new universal constant (~2.4e6) is far worse than those.
caveats: Lean-formalized; universal constant is not optimized.

title: Strong Kadison–Kastler stability and its spatial boundaries
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Two von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space whose unit balls are uniformly close are conjugate by a unitary close to the identity, with a tolerance independent of everything else. Counterexamples show the same fails for one-sided near-inclusions and for separable C*-algebras.
constructive: no: delta(eps) exists but is not explicit. The amenable case has the explicit known-type bound ||v-I|| <= 150*gamma.
explicit_constants: delta(eps) not explicit; amenable near-inclusion has 150*gamma for gamma<1/100
opportunity: None. QUANT was checked and rejected. Finite-dimensional algebras (quantum codes and subsystems) are amenable, and near-identity conjugacy for them was already known with explicit constants (Christensen 1977-80). The new content concerns non-amenable infinite-dimensional factors.
caveats: Main theorem is Lean-formalized.

title: Relative bicentralizers and modular spectral recovery
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Proves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture: every type III_1 factor with separable predual has trivial bicentralizer for every faithful normal state. It also proves a relative version for inclusions with conditional expectations.
constructive: no
opportunity: None. PHYS was checked: local algebras in algebraic QFT are type III_1, but they are hyperfinite, and Haagerup proved the bicentralizer conjecture for that case long ago. No computational content.
caveats: The Lean doc states that the absolute (headline) bicentralizer conjecture is not included in the formalization.

title: Cuntz comparison, nuclear dimension, and equivariant Jiang–Su stability
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Settles regularity questions in the Elliott classification programme: strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability are equivalent, including nonsimple and equivariant versions.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: nuclear dimension of A⊗Z is at most 1 (sharp)
opportunity: None. C*-classification theory has no computational or physical consumer for these regularity statements.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Kirchberg's O_2 norm-ultrapower embedding problem
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: The full group C*-algebra of the explicit group Z[1/2]^3 ⋊ (SL_3(Z) × Z) does not embed unitally into a norm ultrapower of any nuclear C*-algebra, in particular O_2. This answers Kirchberg's question negatively.
constructive: yes: the obstruction group is explicit
opportunity: None. This concerns ultrapower embeddability in C*-algebra model theory. The connection to Connes-embedding-type questions in quantum information (MIP*=RE) runs through tracial von Neumann ultrapowers and quantum correlations, not norm ultrapowers of nuclear algebras, so it does not affect nonlocal-game work.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Invariant projections, hyperinvariant subspaces, and transitive algebras
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Constructs a nonzero quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space with no nontrivial closed subspace invariant under its whole commutant. This solves the hyperinvariant subspace problem negatively. It also gives weighted rotations with no invariant projections in the hyperfinite II_1 factor.
constructive: yes: explicit weighted shifts with ||S||=e^{-10} and ||S^n|| <= exp(-10 floor((n+1)^2/4))
opportunity: None. Invariant-subspace questions in control theory and systems theory are finite-dimensional or concern shift-invariant spaces (Beurling-Lax), where the structure is classical. A quasinilpotent counterexample on infinite-dimensional Hilbert space has no engineering consumer.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Constructs a C*-algebra with normalized 2-quasitraces that are all non-additive, by a fixed margin of 1/144. Consequently two simple stably finite C*-algebras can have a properly infinite tensor product.
constructive: yes: explicit algebra and explicit defect 1/144
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: The Kadison–Ringrose cohomology conjecture
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: All higher bounded Hochschild cohomology groups of a von Neumann algebra with coefficients in itself vanish. Every bounded cocycle of degree at least 2 is a coboundary.
constructive: no
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: The generator problem for finite factors
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Every type II_1 factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator (equivalently by two self-adjoint operators). For irreducible subfactors P⊂M, generic unitaries u satisfy M=W*(P,u).
constructive: no: the generators form a dense G_delta set, so existence comes from a Baire-category argument and Popa's independence theorem; no explicit generator
opportunity: None. Single-generation of II_1 factors does not affect quantum information, which is finite-dimensional, or any numerical representation of operator algebras.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: In ZFC, constructs a nonseparable simple C*-algebra with a faithful trace that has exactly one irreducible representation up to equivalence and is not the compact operators.
constructive: partial: ZFC construction by HNN extensions over a transfinite process; nonseparable
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized. An alternative ZFC construction (Tanaka) exists.

title: Two notions of free entropy differ even when both are finite
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: Constructs a bounded tuple of operators whose microstates free entropy (counting approximating matrices) and non-microstates free entropy (via free Fisher information) are both finite but differ by at least 1/2.
constructive: partial: explicit tuple with a large but unspecified fixed number of variables
opportunity: None. Free entropy appears in random-matrix large deviations, but no applied random-matrix computation (wireless capacity, RMT for learning) uses either free entropy as a tool. Separating the two definitions changes nothing downstream.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion and infinite tensor-power Jiang–Su stability
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: A unital separable C*-algebra absorbs the Jiang–Su algebra exactly when its central-sequence algebra has no characters. Infinite tensor powers of character-free algebras are Jiang–Su stable.
constructive: no
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Approximation and quadratic strong-operator paving
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: This is the Kadison–Singer paving idea moved to arbitrary maximal abelian subalgebras of arbitrary von Neumann algebras. After discarding a piece that is small in the strong-operator sense, any self-adjoint operator can be cut into at most 5e8/eps^2 diagonal blocks whose off-diagonal part has norm at most eps.
constructive: no: colorings come from an existence argument with a mixed-determinantal (interlacing-type) root-sum cost over exponentially many random choices, plus measurable random assignment on a Bernoulli extension. The finite-dimensional input is Ravichandran–Srivastava multipaving (RS17 Thm 25), which is itself existential.
explicit_constants: r_eps = ceil(4e8/eps^2)+ceil(4/eps)+1 <= 5e8 eps^-2 (exponent 2 optimal; constant not optimized); approximation paving C*eps^-6 with C unspecified
opportunity: None beyond existing results. ALGO, COMM and NET were checked and rejected. In finite dimensions (frames, sampling and signal processing, spectral graph sparsification), paving for the diagonal masa was settled by Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava (2015), and the optimal O(eps^-2) multipaving by Ravichandran–Srivastava (2017). This paper uses the latter as a black box and lifts it to infinite, diffuse masas with a constant (4e8) far worse than RS17. The strong-operator compression q lives in M, not A, and is chosen after the test vectors, so it cannot be turned into a usable time-frequency or frame partition. The algorithmic question practitioners care about, polynomial-time Weaver/Kadison–Singer partitions and graph signings, is being worked on separately in human preprints (e.g. arXiv 2609.23855, 2609.17266), not here.
caveats: Not Lean-formalized. The so-paving notion (compression by q near 1 strongly) is weaker than norm paving, which Popa–Vaes showed fails for general masas.

title: Trace cones and Razak–Jacelon stabilization
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: After tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, separable nuclear C*-algebras are classified by their cones of tracial weights.
constructive: no
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: For a minimal homeomorphism, the radius of comparison (a C*-algebra invariant) of the crossed product equals half the mean dimension of the dynamical system. A companion paper proves a complex-cobordism compression theorem used in the proof.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: exact identity rc = mdim/2; compression proportions a/8 with 0<a<1/16
opportunity: None. COMM was checked: mean dimension has a signal-processing link through Lindenstrauss–Tsukamoto/Gutman embeddings of dynamical systems into band-limited signal spaces, with embedding dimension about 2·mdim. This result computes an operator-algebra invariant from mean dimension and does not change any embedding or sampling bound.
caveats: Not Lean-formalized; uses a complex-cobordism companion paper.

title: Weak pure infiniteness and Cuntz-algebra absorption
subject: Operator algebras
plain_english: If every positive element of a C*-algebra is properly infinite, the algebra is strongly purely infinite. For separable nuclear algebras this gives O_infinity absorption.
constructive: no
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Tingley’s sphere-isometry problem
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: Any distance-preserving bijection between the unit spheres of two real Banach spaces extends to a linear isometry of the whole spaces. The sphere's metric determines the space.
constructive: yes: the extension is the explicit formula T(x)=||x|| f(x/||x||); the proof is by contradiction
opportunity: None. Finite-dimensional Tingley cases were already known; the infinite-dimensional general case has no consumer.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Independence of the separable quotient problem
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: Whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient is independent of ZFC (relative to a measurable cardinal). It holds if the continuum is real-valued measurable and fails under CH.
constructive: no: set-theoretic independence
opportunity: None. Only nonseparable spaces of density at least aleph_1 are affected; numerical and applied analysis works in separable spaces.
caveats: Lean-formalized; consistency is relative to a measurable cardinal.

title: Lipschitz equivalent Banach spaces need not be linearly isomorphic
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: There are separable Banach spaces that are bi-Lipschitz equivalent as metric spaces, with explicit distortion constants 4/21 and 76/25, but not linearly isomorphic. Nonlinear geometry does not determine linear structure.
constructive: partial: explicit spaces and bi-Lipschitz map with explicit constants, built on Lipschitz-free space machinery
opportunity: None. GEO was checked and rejected. Metric embedding and sketching work with finite metrics and finite-dimensional normed targets. Whether infinite-dimensional separable spaces can be bi-Lipschitz equivalent without being linearly isomorphic does not affect any distortion bound or algorithm.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: For any square matrix or bounded operator A and any polynomial p, even one with matrix coefficients (P[A]=sum A^j ⊗ B_j), ||P[A]|| <= 2·max over the numerical range W(A)={x*Ax : |x|=1} of ||P(z)||. The best previously published constant was 1+sqrt2 ≈ 2.414 (Crouzeix–Palencia 2017), and 2 cannot be improved.
constructive: partial: the inequality itself is explicit. The structural theorem makes the optimal similarity S=H^{1/2} the minimizer of a small LMI (I ⪯ H ⪯ tau·I, T*HT ⪯ H with T=f(A), f a conformal map from an analytic convex Omega ⊃ W(A) to the disk), so it can be computed for a given matrix. The theorem certifies the optimum kappa <= 2.
explicit_constants: Sharp constant 2: complete, all dimensions, infinite-dimensional Hilbert operators, holomorphic/rational f near closure of W(A). Optimal conformal similarity has cond(S) <= 2.
opportunity: This sharpens the explicit constant in every a-priori bound built on the numerical range (field of values). Scalar bounds improve by a factor 2/(1+sqrt2)=0.828 (17% tighter): GMRES residual ||r_k||/||r_0|| <= C·min_p max_W |p| with C: 2.414→2, and the Arnoldi f(A)b error constant 2C: 4.83→4. For a linear rate rho the bound needs log((1+sqrt2)/2)/|log rho| ≈ 0.19/|log rho| fewer iterations, e.g. 1.8 of ~183 iterations at rho=0.9 and tol 1e-8, about 1%. The complete (matrix-coefficient) form is the drop's unique contribution. Human scalar proofs give 2 only for m=1; Crouzeix–Palencia's complete constant was 1+sqrt2. Two places need it: (i) block Krylov, whose residual sum_j A^j R0 C_j is P[A] with P(z)=sum z^j C_j^T (block GMRES via matrix polynomials, Simoncini–Gallopoulos 1996; block f(A)B methods, Frommer–Lund–Szyld), where the constant goes 2.414→2. This matters only for the sharper min over matrix polynomials; with scalar p(z)·I the scalar theorem already suffices; (ii) Crouzeix–Kressner's bivariate bound for f{A,B} (Fréchet derivatives and condition numbers of matrix functions, Sylvester-type operators, Krylov for f{A,B}c), which multiplies a scalar constant by a complete one. That gives 5.83 published, 4.83 with human scalar-2 results only, and 4 with this theorem. Their nilpotent example shows 4 is sharp, so this closes the problem. Beneficiaries: numerical linear algebra theory and textbooks, a-priori analyses of non-normal quantum eigenvalue processing (Low–Su App. B.2 uses Crouzeix–Palencia), and time-stepping stability bounds when W(hA) lies inside a bounded stability region.
targets: GMRES / Krylov field-of-values convergence bounds (Beckermann 2005 Faber bound; Saad 'Iterative Methods' and Liesen–Strakoš 'Krylov Subspace Methods' textbooks)

Block Krylov bounds via matrix-valued polynomials (Simoncini–Gallopoulos block GMRES 1996; Frommer–Lund–Szyld block Krylov for f(A)B). Complete version needed only for the matrix-polynomial min-max form

Krylov/Arnoldi matrix-function a-priori error bounds (Beckermann–Reichel 2009 Faber-transform bounds; documentation of Güttel's funm_kryl and RKToolbox; expm_multiply and Expokit use a-posteriori estimates, so their docs are not affected)
Bivariate matrix functions, Fréchet derivative and condition bounds (Crouzeix–Kressner arXiv 2007.09784): constant 5.83→4, sharp; Higham Matrix Function Toolbox funm_condest1/expm_cond documentation
Quantum eigenvalue processing for non-normal block-encoded matrices (Low–Su, FOCS 2024, Appendix B.2 'Matrix function bound with Crouzeix–Palencia theorem')
Numerical-range stability of Runge–Kutta / rational time-stepping (power bound when W(hA) lies in a bounded stability region)
Mathlib numerical range / spectral sets (upstream the 0-sorry OAI DirectCrouzeix / NumericalRange development)
first_step: Write a short note restating the standard numerical-range bounds with sharp constants: GMRES and block GMRES 2, Arnoldi f(A)b 4, bivariate f{A,B}/Fréchet 4 (sharp). Check them numerically on the 2x2 Jordan-block extremal and on Crouzeix–Kressner's nilpotent A=B example. Then send the note to Kressner/Beckermann/Güttel and Low–Su to update constants in their bounds and documentation.
caveats: The scalar constant 2 was also proved independently by humans (Lorist–Schwenninger arXiv 2608.03841, Aug 2026, which covers Hilbert-space operators; Jin; Luo), so scalar-level gains are not unique to the drop. Unique to the drop: the complete version in all dimensions (previously known only for base dimension at most 3), Lean formalization, and the optimal-similarity theorem. All gains are constant factors in worst-case a-priori bounds. Production Krylov and expm codes stop on a-posteriori residuals or estimates, so no runtime or code changes follow. Unbounded generators are not covered directly.

title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: A real Banach space with the approximation property is K-convex (has nontrivial type) exactly when it and its dual both have finite cotype.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: uniform decay w_n(T) <= w_{n-2m}(T)/2 for n >= n_0, with n_0 unspecified
opportunity: None. Type/cotype are tools of local Banach-space theory; the characterization does not change any probabilistic or learning bound.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: A Banach space has Markov type p>1, meaning random walks on it spread no faster than in Hilbert space up to a power, exactly when it admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm. This answers Naor's question.
constructive: partial: the proof builds explicit finite reversible chains with linear displacement in non-superreflexive spaces; the result itself is qualitative
opportunity: None practical. GEO was checked: Markov type is a tool for distortion lower bounds (expanders and other finite metrics into Banach targets), and through Ball extension for Lipschitz extension. This theorem is a qualitative characterization of which infinite-dimensional spaces have nontrivial Markov type. It gives no new distortion number for any finite metric used in approximation algorithms.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive Banach spaces
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: Every nonexpansive (1-Lipschitz) self-map of a closed bounded convex set in a reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. This settles Kirk's problem without uniform convexity.
constructive: no: the proof is by contradiction with a Zorn's-lemma minimal invariant set and the Goebel–Karlovitz diametral lemma. It gives no iteration and no rate.
opportunity: None. OPT was checked and rejected. Operator-splitting and fixed-point methods (Krasnoselskii–Mann, Douglas–Rachford, ADMM, PDHG) run in Hilbert or finite-dimensional spaces, where existence (Browder–Göhde–Kirk) and convergence theory were already complete. Reflexive non-uniformly-convex Banach spaces do not occur in practice, and existence without an algorithm adds nothing.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: The number of small cubes needed to cover a symmetric convex body K can be vastly larger, on a log scale, than the number of copies of the polar body needed to cover the polar of the cube. Pietsch's 1972 conjecture that the two covering complexities agree up to universal constants is false.
constructive: yes in principle: an explicit finite-field and graph-distance-profile matrix converted into bodies. Dimensions are astronomically large: theta=1/(1000a) requires h+1 >= 3^{1000a} (h ≈ 10^477 for a=1), then rank r, u ~ 2D_h/theta, a prime p > exp(8bC/D_h) with C ~ 2^u, and dimension n = p^{D_h}·|T|.
explicit_constants: Fully explicit parameter chain, but tower-type; log N(L°,a^{-1}K°)/log N(K,L) <= 2h^2 s/(r+h-1) + 2/r -> 0
opportunity: In learning theory, Hu–Peale–Reingold (ALT 2022) showed that outcome-indistinguishability sample complexity is characterized both by the entropy of the predictor class in the distinguisher-dual norm and by the reverse. They linked this to the duality conjecture and proved a variant with a (M1·M2/eps)^2 loss. The counterexample (Lean-formalized) settles the conjecture HPR called open: no universal-constant duality exists even for symmetric convex classes with an ell_inf covering body. So the scale-dependent losses in such characterizations are necessary, not artifacts of the proofs. My inference: in the natural translation (uniform measure on Y, distinguishers = scaled coordinate indicators), the uniform bound M2 grows with dimension. This redirects a small theory community away from proving dimension-free duality. It does not affect any algorithm.
targets: Outcome indistinguishability / multicalibration sample-complexity theory (Hu–Peale–Reingold, ALT 2022, Thm 11)
Covering-number and metric-entropy arguments in statistical learning theory (dual-norm entropy swaps)
Asymptotic geometric analysis community (Artstein–Milman–Szarek(–Tomczak-Jaegermann) entropy-duality programme)
first_step: Restate the counterexample in function-class language: F1=K, distinguishers = scaled ell_1 ball, uniform measure on Y. Record which parameter (M2 ~ dimension) must blow up, and post this as a remark/erratum to the HPR duality discussion so OI papers stop citing the universal-constant duality as plausible.
caveats: Asymptotic in dimension with tower-type sizes, so not usable as benchmark instances. It says nothing about fixed dimension or natural function classes. Known positive cases stand: one body an ellipsoid (AMS 2004), bounded K-convexity constant, convexified packing.

title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: The Lipschitz-free space over a metric space is the completion of finitely supported signed measures under the Kantorovich–Rubinstein (Wasserstein-1 / Earth Mover's) norm. The paper builds a countable metric space with all distances at least 1 whose free space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property: no uniformly bounded finite-rank maps approximate the identity.
constructive: partial: explicit colored random-regular-graph blocks with anchors (diam <= 300p^2+150p+5) chosen by a deterministic-sequence plus local-convergence argument. The obstruction is a proof by contradiction over all finite-rank operators.
explicit_constants: block diameter B_p=300p^2+150p+5; norm-p finite-rank maps miss some delta_a by >= 1/2; ell_1 renorming with 2B_p-BAP but not p-BAP
opportunity: None. GEO (EMD sketching and embedding) was checked and rejected. For any finite metric space the free space is finite-dimensional, and the identity is itself a finite-rank norm-1 map, so the obstruction disappears for every input an EMD sketch (Indyk–Thaper grids, quadtree/tree embeddings, Sinkhorn, Wasserstein-1 linear sketches) actually sees. The phenomenon needs countably infinite blocks. Known EMD sketching limits (e.g. Naor–Schechtman non-embeddability of grid EMD into L1) are unaffected.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Reflexive midpoint convexity and diamond distortion
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: Constructs reflexive Banach spaces whose norm is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex but that admit no asymptotically uniformly convex renorming. In these spaces, depth-k countably branching diamond graphs need distortion at least sqrt(1+k/12).
constructive: yes: explicit tree and segment norms with explicit moduli
explicit_constants: moduli >= sqrt(1+t^2/12)-1; diamond distortion D^2 >= 1+k/12 (or 1+k/4 in companions)
opportunity: None. GEO was checked and rejected. Finite diamond graphs matter for L1 embedding lower bounds and flow-cut gaps (Newman–Rabinovich, Lee–Raghavendra), but this concerns countably branching diamonds in exotic reflexive spaces and asymptotic renorming theory. No distortion bound for a finite metric used in algorithms changes.
caveats: Lean formalization covers the headline diamond bound; 22 companion inputs are assumed in some graph deductions.

title: Metric Markov cotype of ℓ1 and Hilbert-space Lipschitz extension
subject: Functional analysis
plain_english: ell_1 has metric Markov cotype 2 with constant at most 12·sqrt21 ≈ 55: values on a reversible Markov chain can be smoothed at controlled cost. Via Ball/Mendel–Naor, any Lipschitz map from a subset of Hilbert space into ell_1 extends to the whole space with only a universal constant-factor loss. This answers Ball's 1992 extension question for this target.
constructive: partial: the Markov-cotype witnesses are explicit, y_i = E[coordinatewise median of x_{J1},x_{J2},x_{J3}] with J_a independent endpoints of a geometric-time walk. The extension corollary goes through the Ball/Mendel–Naor duality theorem, which is non-constructive, although for finite point sets an optimal ell_1^d-valued extension is a linear program.
explicit_constants: N_2(ell_1) <= 12·sqrt21 (squared 3024); extension constant K universal but not computed (a universal multiple of N_2 via Mendel–Naor Cor. 1.13)
opportunity: The paper does not mention this, but it follows by plugging Corollary 1.13 into an existing reduction. Makarychev–Makarychev (FOCS 2010, Thm 5.7/Cor 5.9) proved that the best cut-sparsifier quality on k terminals satisfies Q_k^cut = e_k(ell_1,ell_1) <= O(e(ell_2,ell_1)·sqrt(log k)·log log k), conditional on Ball's question (finite e(ell_2,ell_1)). This paper answers that question. So every graph with k terminals has a terminal-only cut sparsifier of quality O(sqrt(log k)·log log k). That improves the long-standing O(log k/log log k) upper bound and meets the Ω(sqrt(log k)/log log k) lower bound (Johnson–Schechtman–Figiel) up to (log log k)^2, essentially settling the existential question. It benefits vertex-sparsification and terminal-cut approximation theory (e.g. approximation ratios for balanced or sparsest cut that depend on k instead of n).
targets: Vertex/cut sparsification theory (Moitra; Leighton–Moitra; Charikar–Leighton–Li–Moitra; Makarychev–Makarychev FOCS 2010)
Terminal-based approximation algorithms (balanced/sparsest cut on terminal sets, multicommodity flow-cut problems)
first_step: Check MMMR Thm 5.7 and later sparsifier literature (2016–2026) for any newer upper bound. Then write up the corollary Q_k^cut = O(sqrt(log k)·log log k) with an explicit constant. Pose the algorithmic question: a polynomial-time Õ(sqrt(log k)) cut sparsifier via ALN embedding plus an LP for ell_1-valued Lipschitz extension.
caveats: Existential only: the extension comes from a duality argument and MMMR's quality-e_k sparsifiers are existential, while their polynomial-time flow sparsifiers stay at O(log k/log log k). The asymptotic gain is galactic: ignoring the unknown K, sqrt(L)·log L < L/log L only once L=log k exceeds about 5500. Not Lean-formalized, but the proof is short and elementary (~650 lines).

title: Serre’s intersection-multiplicity conjecture
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Take two modules over a regular local ring that meet only at the closed point and have complementary dimensions. Serre's alternating-Tor intersection multiplicity of the pair is always strictly positive. This now includes ramified mixed characteristic.
constructive: no: a positivity proof built on perfectoid normalized lengths, Galois averaging and Land–Tamme K-theoretic descent; it gives no new computation
opportunity: None. Macaulay2 and Singular compute intersection multiplicities via Tor for polynomial and equicharacteristic inputs, where positivity has been Serre's theorem since 1965. The only new case is ramified mixed-characteristic regular local rings, which never come up in applied computation. The symbolic-power corollary (P∩Q^(r) ⊆ m^{r+1}) is also pure.
caveats: Not formalized; this is a 60-year-old conjecture settled with heavy perfectoid and K-theory machinery. The paper's footnote mentions a competing AI-assisted public claim (Editan, Dec 2025).

title: Lech’s multiplicity conjecture
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity, which measures how singular a local ring is, never decreases along a flat local homomorphism.
constructive: no: an inequality proved by reductions plus normalized-length and Dutta-multiplicity comparisons in each characteristic
opportunity: None. Singular (`mult`) and Macaulay2 (`multiplicity`/`degree`) compute multiplicities. No algorithm or applied workflow uses a comparison across flat local maps.
caveats: Lean covers only a supporting characteristic-p Dutta-multiplicity lemma, not the full theorem. This is a major open conjecture (Lech 1960).

title: A counterexample to the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture
subject: Algebra
plain_english: The ring is the completed vertex of the section-ring cone over an explicit Hirzebruch–Kummer cover surface (n=7). It is a 3-dimensional complete normal local domain over C with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module.
constructive: partial: the ring is explicit (section ring of a specified surface and polarization); nonexistence follows from the numerical obstruction K^2−2c2 > 6H^2
opportunity: None. Small MCM modules matter only inside the homological-conjectures programme. Macaulay2 tools for matrix factorizations and Ulrich modules work on small hypersurfaces or curves, not on degree-1715 section rings, so no test instance or software change follows.
caveats: Lean only checks that the candidate ring is a complete normal local domain, not the nonexistence. Overlaps with recent AI-assisted preprints by Anghel and Chen.
