title: A counterexample to Kaplansky’s zero-divisor conjecture
subject: Algebra
plain_english: This refutes Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture. It gives a finitely presented torsion-free group G with nonzero α, β in the group algebra F2[G] and αβ = 0.
constructive: partial: random construction over PG(2,128) labels (16516-letter alphabet, 8258 generators) with graphs on n vertices, n a multiple of 2·16513^2 ≈ 5.5×10^8 and 'sufficiently large'; no explicit presentation is ever produced
explicit_constants: q=128, v=16513, |T|=16516; n ≥ 5.5×10^8 and otherwise ineffective
opportunity: None. I checked the CAS/INSTANCES channel. Gardam's SAT-based unit searches and the Garg–Mineyev computations look for small-support zero divisors or units in specific small groups (Promislow/Hantzsche–Wendt, Ã₂ lattices). This group has more than 8000 generators and supports of size at least about 5×10^8, so it is not a test instance and says nothing about where small searches should look. Group-ring cryptosystems use finite groups (torsion), which this result does not touch.
caveats: The top line is Lean-formalized. The object is astronomically large and random.

title: A torsion-free group algebra that is not directly finite
subject: Algebra
plain_english: These are group algebras over finite fields with ab = 1 but ba ≠ 1. There are versions over F2 with a torsion-free finitely presented group, in characteristic 2 with odd torsion, and in odd characteristic; all the groups are therefore nonsofic. Consequences: injective but non-surjective cellular automata (refuting Gottschalk's conjecture), and an integer group-ring matrix whose Fuglede–Kadison determinant lies in (0,1).
constructive: partial: char-2 version is a 'terminating prescription' that 'has not been executed' and 'need not be computationally practical'; odd-char version uses p = least prime factor of (C(1200,600)!)^2+1
explicit_constants: odd case: |K| = p^4 with p dividing (C(1200,600)!)^2+1 (never evaluated); F2 torsion-free case inherits the random-graph sizes of 196
opportunity: None. Three channels checked. (1) Cellular automata: the counterexample automaton lives on a nonsofic group. Practical CA (Z^d lattices, Golly, CA-based PRNG/crypto proposals) use amenable groups, where the Garden-of-Eden and surjunctivity theorems still hold. (2) L² invariants: L²-Betti and L²-torsion computations via Lück approximation are done for residually finite or sofic groups, where the Determinant Conjecture is a theorem. (3) The first finitely presented nonsofic group is a major structural fact (its labelled Cayley graph is not a Benjamini–Schramm limit of finite graphs), but it changes no computation.
caveats: Lean covers the char-2, odd-char and determinant top lines. Nonsoficity is a one-line deduction via Elek–Szabó and is outside Lean scope.

title: A counterexample to finitistic-dimension finiteness
subject: Algebra
plain_english: This refutes the little finitistic-dimension conjecture. One fixed finite-dimensional complex algebra has finitely generated modules of finite but unboundedly large projective dimension.
constructive: partial: A = D ⋉ X is fixed and is obtained by a three-stage realization of a selection process on a finitely presented group algebra, but its quiver and dimension are never written down
explicit_constants: pd N_m ≥ 2m−2; algebra size not stated
opportunity: None. QPA (GAP) computes projective resolutions for explicit small quiver algebras. This algebra is not given in a usable explicit form, and no applied area relies on finitistic-dimension bounds.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Counterexamples to Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa and related homological conjectures
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Explicit finite-dimensional algebras over F2(q,H1,H2) carry a nonprojective module with no positive self-extensions and no extensions into the algebra. This refutes the Auslander–Reiten conjecture, the Gorenstein-projective conjecture and Tachikawa's second conjecture. The associated endomorphism algebra also refutes the Nakayama and Auslander–Gorenstein conjectures.
constructive: yes: C (dim 10) → T = C⋉DC (dim 20) → A = T⊗T (dim 400) → Λ of dim 800+dim F, with an explicit Hochschild cocycle table (18^4 = 104976 finite checks)
opportunity: None. I checked the INSTANCES angle and rejected it. QPA (GAP) computes Ext over finite fields and Q. This example needs transcendental parameters (H1/H2 must have infinite multiplicative order), so it does not specialize to any finite field. Vanishing in every Ext degree also cannot be confirmed by finite computation.
caveats: The AR and Tachikawa top lines are Lean-formalized.

title: Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Over any characteristic-0 field, take a homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence of degrees a_1,…,a_c. It has the same Hilbert function as an explicit monomial 'lex-plus-powers' ideal (lex segment plus x_i^{a_i}), and every graded Betti number is at most that ideal's.
constructive: partial: the extremal LPP ideal is explicit and computable from the Hilbert function; the proof itself is an existence argument via commuting linear forms over a division algebra over a finitely generated extension of C
opportunity: This is the only algebra result here that touches commutative-algebra software, and only slightly. Over char-0 fields: (i) a Hilbert function is realizable by S/I with I containing a regular sequence of degrees a exactly when it is realized by a quotient of k[x]/(x_i^{a_i}), which the Clements–Lindström growth condition decides; (ii) the LPP ideal bounds every graded Betti number in advance. Macaulay2's LexIdeals package already ships `LPP`, `isLPP` and `generateLPPs`, but its docs still say LPP ideals are 'conjectured' to play the lex-ideal role. Those docs could be updated and a realizability predicate added. I checked the coding-theory channel: EGH Cayley–Bacharach statements bound minimum distance and hyp_I(d) for evaluation codes on complete-intersection point sets (Tohăneanu–Van Tuyl; Cooper–Seceleanu–Tohăneanu–Vaz Pinto–Villarreal 2020). That channel fails because codes live over F_q and this proof is char 0 only. Gröbner-basis cryptanalysis over F_q is blocked for the same reason.
first_step: Propose a documentation note for the LexIdeals `LPP` node (and optionally an `isLPPHilbertFunction(a,h)` helper based on Clements–Lindström) that cites the char-0 claim as unrefereed.
caveats: Char 0 only; positive characteristic, the case coding and cryptanalysis need, stays open. Not formalized, and spread over two long companion papers on a classic conjecture. Gives extremal bounds, not an algorithmic speedup.
evidence: Macaulay2 LexIdeals docs (LPP node: 'conjectured to play a role analogous...')

title: A counterexample to Kurosh’s division-ring problem
subject: Algebra
plain_english: A countable characteristic-0 division ring is generated by two elements over its center, every element is algebraic, and yet it is infinite-dimensional over the center.
constructive: no: built by scheduling all polynomial expressions in a countable diagonal lifting construction; not an explicit object
opportunity: None. I checked COMM: space-time block codes (perfect codes) use finite-dimensional cyclic division algebras over number fields, which this infinite-dimensional object does not affect.
caveats: Not formalized; long (150KB); resolves the 1941 Kurosh problem.

title: The blockwise Alperin weight conjecture
subject: Algebra
plain_english: For every finite group and prime p, the number of irreducible Brauer characters in each p-block equals the number of conjugacy classes of its 'weights', which are local data attached to p-subgroups.
constructive: no: an equality of counts from block-algebra traces and divisibility of tuple counts via covers of genus-one curves in mixed characteristic
opportunity: None. I checked CAS (GAP/Magma modular representation theory, Modular Atlas). l(B) is already computable from the ordinary character table as the rank of Irr(B) restricted to p-regular classes. Weight counts need classification of radical p-subgroups, which is harder. The theorem therefore offers no cheaper route; at most it removes 'assuming AWC' hedges in a few verification papers.
caveats: This is an extraordinary claim: a proof of AWC that avoids the classification of finite simple groups (CFSG), via arithmetic geometry. It is not formalized and is long (215KB). Treat with caution.
evidence: /root/openai-math/preprints/The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-September-23-2026/build/sections/intro.tex (Thm thm:main, prior work, counting problem and curve construction)

title: Donovan's conjecture over fields and complete mixed-characteristic DVRs
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Blocks of finite groups whose defect groups have bounded order fall into finitely many Morita-equivalence classes, over a fixed algebraically closed field of characteristic p and over complete DVRs such as W(F̄_p).
constructive: no: finiteness with no explicit bound on the number of classes
opportunity: None. The only computational touchpoint is the classification of Morita classes of blocks with small defect groups (Eaton's Block Library). An ineffective finiteness theorem tells those classifiers neither when a list is complete nor what is missing.
caveats: Not formalized (about 437KB of TeX). It relies on the coefficient comparison from 202, which is also unformalized.

title: Tensor saturation for even spin groups
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Take Spin(2n) and three dominant weights whose sum lies in the root lattice. If some dilation Nλ, Nμ, Nν has a tensor invariant, then λ, μ, ν already do. This is the Kapovich–Millson saturation conjecture with factor 1 in type D.
constructive: no for the theorem; it does yield an algorithmic consequence (see opportunity)
opportunity: This is a non-obvious ALGO channel. With saturation factor 1 plus the root-lattice condition, a Spin(2n) tensor invariant exists exactly when the rational Berenstein–Zelevinsky (or Littelmann) polytope for (λ,μ,ν) is nonempty. That is LP feasibility, so positivity of type-D tensor multiplicities is decidable in polynomial time. The GCT3 argument (Mulmuley–Narayanan–Sohoni: Littlewood–Richardson positivity is in P via Knutson–Tao saturation) explicitly said it did not extend to types B, C, D; it now extends to D. Current tools (LiE, SageMath WeylCharacterRing, LieART) compute full decompositions, at a cost that grows with the weights. The beneficiaries are a small group: representation-theory and Horn-problem researchers for so(2n), plus model builders, who usually want multiplicities rather than positivity.
first_step: Write down the type-D_n BZ polytope inequalities, implement 'positivity = root-lattice check + LP feasibility' in Sage, and cross-check against LiE tensor decompositions for n ≤ 8 with random large weights.
caveats: The paper does not state the algorithm. Polytope-size and lattice details for type D still need checking. The test decides positivity only, not multiplicities. Types B and C remain at factor 2. Not formalized, though it agrees with the known Spin(8), Spin(10) and Spin(12) cases.
evidence: /root/openai-math/preprints/Tensor-Saturation-for-Even-Spin-Groups-September-24-2026/build/sections/01-introduction.tex (Thm thm:main, prior factor-2/4 results, proof outline)
arXiv cs/0501076 (GCT3: 'proof does not generalize... saturation false for B, C, D')

title: Saxl’s conjecture and universal tensor squares
subject: Algebra
plain_english: The tensor square of the staircase irreducible representation of S_n contains every irreducible (Saxl). More generally, for every n other than 2, 4 and 9, some irreducible representation of S_n has a tensor square containing all irreducibles.
constructive: yes: explicit partitions (staircase or modified staircase); degrees n ≤ 64 certified by a C++ mod-p computation of the whole Kronecker-coefficient vector
explicit_constants: finite range n ≤ 64 by computer (about 117 s at n = 64); large n by explicit constructions
opportunity: None. Two requested channels were checked and rejected. (a) GCT: occurrence obstructions need vanishing of Kronecker or plethysm coefficients, and Bürgisser–Ikenmeyer–Panova already ruled them out for permanent vs determinant, so a universal-positivity result gives no lower bound. (b) Quantum marginal problem: positivity of g(ρ_m,ρ_m,ν) just places rational points inside the Kronecker polytope, which Klyachko's inequalities already describe. Minor point: the verifier (a whole-vector Murnaghan–Nakayama recursion modulo 10^9+7) produces g(λ,λ,·) residues for all 1.7M partitions of 64 in about 2 minutes. That is a handy research tool, but it certifies only nonvanishing.
caveats: Both top lines are fully Lean-formalized.

title: Finite lattice representation and undecidability
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Some finite lattices are not the congruence lattice of any finite algebra, and no algorithm can decide which ones are. Recognizing full subgroup intervals [H,G] of finite groups is also undecidable.
constructive: partial: the positive side is an effective semi-decision (colored-graph search, Lean-formalized). The minimal nonrepresentable lattice is pinned down via a Busy Beaver constant that is never evaluated, and the nonrepresentable family comes from Larsen–Pink-type bounds
explicit_constants: |L_0| > 7, otherwise defined via Busy Beaver; every lattice with at most 7 elements is representable (L_7 = [PGL2(F2), PGL2(F64)])
opportunity: None in practice. The only consumers are universal-algebra research tools: UACalc and GAP searches over subgroup intervals in the style of DeMeo's work. Small lattices remain representable, and any nonrepresentable lattice is astronomically large, so such searches are unaffected; only the hope of a complete decision procedure is gone. Algebraic CSP algorithms never need congruence-lattice representability.
caveats: Lean formalizes only the graph criterion, not the undecidability. The companion negative-solution paper is not formalized.

title: The ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for all discrete groups
subject: Algebra
plain_english: For any group, the Hattori–Stallings traces of idempotent matrices over C[G] and over ℓ¹(G) live only on finitely many conjugacy classes of finite-order elements. Consequently, for torsion-free G, group rings over char-0 domains have no idempotents other than 0 and 1.
constructive: no
opportunity: None. This is K-theory of group rings and Banach algebras, with no computational or applied consumer.
caveats: Lean covers the complex Bass trace conjecture and the char-0 Kaplansky idempotent statement.

title: Finite symmetric tensor categories and the Verlinde tower
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Every finite symmetric tensor category in characteristic p has a fiber functor to some higher Verlinde category Ver_{p^n}, so it is a representation category of a group scheme inside that category.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: level n depends on the category
opportunity: None. Tensor categories reach applications through characteristic-0 modular and fusion categories (anyon models for topological quantum computation), not through symmetric categories in characteristic p.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: Integral counterexamples to Gersten’s conjecture
subject: Algebra
plain_english: Explicit two-dimensional ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic (0,5), for example V[x,y]/(5+x^4+y^4) localized, have nonzero K_3 and K_5 classes that vanish over the fraction field.
constructive: yes: the rings are explicit; the classes are detected mod 5
explicit_constants: V = unramified degree-8 extension of Z_5; relation 5 + x^4 + y^4
opportunity: None. Higher algebraic K-theory of ramified regular local rings has no applied or computational consumer.
caveats: Not formalized; plausible.

title: Foulkes' conjecture for sixth powers and quadratic stabilization
subject: Algebra
plain_english: For b ≥ 6, Sym^6(Sym^b V) embeds GL(V)-equivariantly in Sym^b(Sym^6 V). More generally, the canonical Foulkes–Howe multiplication map Sym^b(Sym^a V) → Sym^a(Sym^b V) is surjective once b ≥ a(a−1), in every dimension of V.
constructive: partial: the canonical map is explicit; the finite range 6 ≤ b ≤ 29 is closed by certified C++ multiplicity computations
explicit_constants: b ≥ a(a−1), a polynomial bound that answers Landsberg's GCT-survey Problem 7.19
opportunity: None for practice. The GCT link is real but stays inside theory. For b ≥ a(a−1), the coordinate ring of the Chow variety of products of linear forms agrees with its normalization in degree b, and its GL-multiplicities are exactly the plethysm coefficients of Sym^a(Sym^b V). That can tidy multiplicity bookkeeping in GCT papers on orbit closures of x1⋯xn, but it gives no occurrence obstruction or circuit lower bound (compare family 108). The quantum-marginal channel does not apply.
caveats: Lean covers quadratic stabilization and the a = 6 case for b ≥ 30. The range 6 ≤ b ≤ 29 rests on computer certificates.

title: Cannon's conjecture
subject: Group theory
plain_english: Every hyperbolic group whose boundary is a 2-sphere acts geometrically on hyperbolic 3-space. Torsion-free ones are therefore fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds.
constructive: no: a modulus bound plus Bourdon–Kleiner uniformization and Sullivan–Tukia straightening
opportunity: None. I checked the algorithmic channel. Given a word-problem solution, recognizing closed hyperbolic 3-manifold groups is already decidable unconditionally (Groves–Manning–Wilton, using geometrization). 3-manifold software such as SnapPy and Regina works from triangulations and never depends on Cannon's conjecture.
caveats: Lean-formalized top line.

title: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group and a finitely presented nil algebra
subject: Group theory
plain_english: An infinite group with an ordinary finite presentation in which every element has finite order. It is a Steinberg group St_12(R) over an F2-algebra and has property (T); a finite-index subgroup is a residually finite 2-group. The same construction gives finitely presented nil algebras that are not nilpotent.
constructive: partial: the presentation is built from self-simulating rule tables over alphabets of size up to 2^{10000h}, with h ≥ h_0 never specified
explicit_constants: c = 10000, k = 10 in the hierarchy proposition; h_0 is ineffective
opportunity: None. I checked the CAS test-instance angle. GAP, ACE, kbmag and Magma could in principle use an infinite periodic finitely presented group as a stress test for coset enumeration or Knuth–Bendix, but this presentation is astronomically large and is never written out.
caveats: Lean covers the periodic group; the nil-algebra claims are outside Lean scope.

title: Thompson's group F is nonamenable
subject: Group theory
plain_english: Thompson's group F (dyadic piecewise-linear homeomorphisms of [0,1]) has no invariant mean. Equivalently, it has no Følner sets: every finite subset moves a fixed fraction of itself under some element of a fixed finite set.
constructive: partial: explicit Følner-defect lower bound (δ²/L² − 4/D)/(4(1−1/D)) for a finite transport set S that depends on D; nothing is given for the standard generators x0, x1
explicit_constants: δ = 1/2 from an explicit Lipschitz map on L²([0,1];R²); L and D not instantiated; no cogrowth or spectral-radius number for standard generators (the Lean doc also says no explicit constant)
opportunity: No applied action. Three channels checked. (1) Group-based crypto: F was proposed as a platform (Shpilrain–Ushakov 2005) and those schemes were broken by length-based and other attacks. Nonamenability implies random words have linearly growing normal-form length (positive speed), which neither revives nor newly breaks anything. (2) Numerical group theory: it confirms the Elder–Rechnitzer–Janse van Rensburg–Wong cogrowth extrapolations (growth constant about 15 < 16) and closes that computational line. (3) Percolation (p_c < p_u on Cayley graphs of F, via 214) and non-unitarizable representations (via 251) are pure corollaries.
caveats: Lean-formalized with a short proof (36KB). This is the cleanest result in the group-theory half.

title: A finitely generated Eilenberg–Ganea counterexample
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A finitely generated, residually finite group has cohomological dimension 2 but admits no 2-dimensional classifying space. It is a Bestvina–Brady height kernel of a right-angled Artin group (RAAG) built over an explicit acyclic 2-complex.
constructive: yes: explicit seed presentation <x,y | x^2=y^5, x^2=(xy^{-1})^3>; the group is finitely generated but not finitely presented
opportunity: None. This is classifying-space topology, with no computational or applied consumer, and the group is not finitely presented.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Boone–Higman embeddings with higher finiteness
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A finitely generated group has a solvable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group, which can even be taken of type F∞. A single F∞ group also contains every finitely presented group.
constructive: partial: an effective 'compiler' turns a word-problem decider into a finite monoid or group presentation (Higman-style); the sizes are huge and never stated
opportunity: None. Higman-type embeddings are tools for proving undecidability. Nothing in GAP, Magma or formal verification uses them, and the simple overgroups are not practical objects.
caveats: Lean-formalized (all three statements, with a ComputablePred word-problem definition).

title: Amenability, unitarizability, and strong Ulam stability
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A discrete group is amenable exactly when every uniformly bounded Hilbert-space representation is similar to a unitary one (Dixmier). A countable group is amenable exactly when every sufficiently accurate unitary 'almost representation', on any Hilbert space and in operator norm uniformly over the group, is close to a true representation.
constructive: partial: for nonamenable groups it builds explicit unstable almost-representations from boundary-action markings, with a 1/10 distance gap
explicit_constants: distance > 1/10; nonunitarizable representation with bound ≤ 1+ε (separable witness with bound 101)
opportunity: None. I checked QUANT and rejected it. Self-testing and nonlocal-game rigidity use Gowers–Hatami-type stability: finite or amenable groups, normalized Hilbert–Schmidt norm, finite dimensions, and relations checked on generators. Uniform operator-norm stability over the whole group on infinite-dimensional spaces is not a property those protocols rely on, so the new instability direction redirects nobody.
caveats: Lean covers Dixmier and the nonunitarizable witnesses.

title: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is neither residually finite nor linear over any field
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A torsion-free word-hyperbolic group, the fundamental group of a finite Euclidean triangle complex, in which some fixed nontrivial element dies in every finite quotient and in every finite-dimensional linear representation over any field.
constructive: partial: the complex comes from random affine lines over a large prime q, and the argument is existential ('one fixed member of a finite family' works, unidentified)
opportunity: None. I checked group-based crypto. Platform groups with no faithful linear representation would resist linear-representation attacks of the kind that broke braid-group schemes via Lawrence–Krammer. But attacks only need a useful non-faithful image, this group is not explicit, and hyperbolic-group crypto proposals are not deployed.
caveats: Lean-formalized (non-residual-finiteness; nonlinearity is a corollary outside Lean scope).

title: An infinite finitely presented simple amenable group
subject: Group theory
plain_english: There is a group that is simultaneously infinite, finitely presented, simple and amenable. It is an alternating subgroup of a polygon-exchange group on sufficiently many squares.
constructive: partial: finite generators and relators exist, but 'no uniform bound on their sizes is needed'
opportunity: None. A pure existence question in group theory, with no computational or applied use.
caveats: Lean-formalized top line.

title: Classifying spaces and geometric obstructions for Artin groups
subject: Group theory
plain_english: For every Artin group with finitely many generators, the following hold. The Salvetti complex is a K(π,1), giving a finite classifying space, torsion-freeness and center Z^k. Intersections of parabolic subgroups are parabolic. The word and parabolic-membership problems are decidable by an explicit uniform algorithm. Separately, an explicit Artin group on 116 generators has no geometric CAT(0) action.
constructive: yes for the algorithm: a finite graded algebra Z over Q(ζ_N) built from Temperley–Lieb–Jones fusion data, a braid action by complexes of projectives, and Gaussian-elimination cancellation to a minimal complex (Cor. cor:membership). The K(π,1) statement is a contractibility proof
explicit_constants: No complexity bound is asserted. The algebra has (|S|+2)·∏_e(m_e−1) unfolded vertices over edges with label ≥ 4, which is exponential in that edge count. Complex size probably grows exponentially with word length (compare Khovanov–Seidel intersection numbers)
opportunity: There are two concrete CAS wins. (1) GAP HAP's `ResolutionArtin(D)` (Salvetti/Squier resolution for general Coxeter diagrams) is documented as valid only 'in those cases where the [K(π,1)] conjecture is known to hold'. The Lean-formalized theorem makes integral (co)homology computations unconditional for every finite-rank Artin group. SageMath's `ArtinGroup` docs likewise list torsion-freeness, the center, a solvable word problem and K(π,1) as conjectures 'known when the Artin group is finite type and a number of other cases'. (2) This is the first uniform word-problem and parabolic-membership algorithm for all Artin groups. Sage's general `ArtinGroup` falls back to GAP finitely-presented-group (fp-group) methods, which need not terminate. Existing efficient algorithms cover only spherical type (Garside normal forms), large type (Holt–Rees) and diagrams without A3/B3 subdiagrams (quadratic time, Blasco-García et al. 2026). The beneficiaries are geometric group theorists and the HAP and Sage maintainers. Braid-group cryptography (spherical type) gains nothing, because Garside normal forms are already polynomial.
targets: GAP HAP: ResolutionArtin, ResolutionArtinGroup, CoxeterDiagramIsSpherical (aboutArtinGroups page)
GAP/Magma fp-group word problem for Artin groups
first_step: Open a HAP issue proposing to drop the K(π,1) caveat for `ResolutionArtin`, citing the formalized comparator OAI.HarmonicArtin.salvetti_cover_contractible, and propose the matching Sage docstring change. In parallel, prototype the Section 8 membership algorithm in Sage for a small non-FC diagram (labels 4 and ∞) and measure complex growth against word length.
caveats: The K(π,1), parabolic-intersection and CAT(0) top lines are Lean-formalized. The algorithmic corollary is outside Lean scope, and the paper claims no complexity bound. Expect exponential blow-up in word length and in the number of label≥4 edges, so the existing normal-form algorithms will be much faster wherever they apply. Maintainers may hesitate to change documentation on the strength of unrefereed preprints.

title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups
subject: Group theory
plain_english: Any finitely generated group with the same large-scale geometry as a virtually polycyclic group is itself virtually polycyclic, and virtually a uniform lattice in a solvable Lie group (Eskin–Fisher–Whyte conjecture).
constructive: no: a quasi-isometric rigidity statement
opportunity: None. There is no algorithm here. GAP's Polycyclic package works with presentations already known to be polycyclic and has no use for quasi-isometry data.
caveats: Lean-formalized.

title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
subject: Group theory
plain_english: Take a finite system of equations with coefficients in any group whose exponent-sum matrix has full rank over Q. It always has a solution in some larger group (Howie's conjecture). Adding one generator and one relator can never kill a nontrivial group (Kervaire's conjecture).
constructive: no: proves that G embeds in the quotient (spectral-phase and planar-surface argument); no solution is computed
opportunity: None. Equation solvers (Makanin–Razborov-type solvers for free groups, Diophantine problems in group-based crypto) look for solutions inside a given group. This result only guarantees solutions in some unspecified overgroup.
caveats: Lean covers the unimodular Kervaire statement; Howie's multi-equation version is not formalized.

title: A hyperbolic group without a geometric CAT(0) action
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A word-hyperbolic group with a finite 2-dimensional classifying space has no geometric action on any proper CAT(0) space, so no finite model of it carries a locally CAT(0) or CAT(−1) metric.
constructive: no: 'an existence argument [that] does not give an effective size'
opportunity: None. This is pure geometric group theory.
caveats: Lean-formalized (except the 2-dimensionality refinement).

title: Gersten’s conjecture and virtual compact specialness of one-relator groups
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A one-relator group is word-hyperbolic exactly when it contains no Baumslag–Solitar subgroup BS(m,n). Hyperbolic one-relator groups are virtually compact special, hence linear over Z and virtually free-by-cyclic.
constructive: no: a structural dichotomy with no algorithm and no bounds
opportunity: Weak CAS channel. In practice, hyperbolicity of one-relator groups is checked with kbmag, GAP walrus and small-cancellation tests; for example, the Cashen–Hoffmann census (rank 2–4, relator length ≤ 16) records a 'hyperbolicreason' per entry. Gersten's dichotomy suggests a two-sided procedure. One side runs a hyperbolicity semi-decision (Papasoglu, kbmag). The other searches for Baumslag–Solitar witnesses (a b^m a^{-1} = b^n with [a,b] ≠ 1), checked with Magnus's word-problem algorithm. Whether Z² = BS(1,1) witnesses can be certified, and hence whether hyperbolicity is decidable for one-relator groups, needs real research. If it works, it could settle the irank-2 census entries.
first_step: Determine whether every non-hyperbolic one-relator group has a Baumslag–Solitar witness certifiable by the Magnus word-problem solver. Then run a witness search on irank-2 census entries that kbmag and walrus leave unclassified.
caveats: Not formalized and very long (about 760KB of TeX across two papers). The decision-procedure consequence is my inference, not the paper's claim. kbmag already verifies many cases.

title: A group without fixed price
subject: Group theory
plain_english: A finitely generated group, an amalgam of a free group of rank 100 with a direct product, has two free measure-preserving actions whose 'costs' differ. The cost is the average number of edges needed per point to connect orbits.
constructive: yes for the group: Γ = F(a,b1..b99) *_J (J × Z); the cost gap is proved, not computed
explicit_constants: rank-100 free factor; Bernoulli cost bounded away from 1 (no explicit gap stated in the abstract)
opportunity: None. Cost belongs to measured group theory and orbit equivalence, and has no applied consumer.
caveats: Not formalized.

title: Koebe's circle-domain conjecture
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Every planar domain, even one with uncountably many holes, can be conformally mapped to a domain whose holes are round disks or points. Such maps are rigid when the boundary is conformally removable.
constructive: no (existence via exhaustion/compactness)
opportunity: Numerical conformal mapping to circle domains (Schottky-Klein prime-function methods, multiply connected potential flow, circle packing software) only handles finitely many holes, where Koebe's theorem has been classical since about 1920. Countably many holes were already settled by He-Schramm. The new uncountable-boundary case has no computational counterpart.

title: Brennan's conjecture and the integral-means spectrum
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: If phi maps a simply connected domain conformally onto the disk, then |phi'|^s is area-integrable for every 4/3<s<4. This settles a sharp universal integral-means exponent.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: sharp exponents; strict B_b(-1)<1/4 with unspecified margin
opportunity: In principle, integrability of conformal-map derivatives feeds into error analysis of numerical conformal mapping and polynomial approximation on rough domains. No method's practical convergence depends on the endpoint exponents settled here.

title: The Falconer distance conjecture
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Any compact set in R^d with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2 has a set of pairwise distances with positive length (positive Lebesgue measure).
constructive: no
opportunity: This is fractal geometric measure theory with no algorithmic or engineering consumer. Finite-point distance problems such as Erdos distinct distances are different statements.

title: Kakeya in three and four dimensions
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Sets containing a unit segment in every direction must be 'full-dimensional' (dimension 4 in R^4), and the 3D Kakeya maximal operator has the conjectured L^3 bound up to delta^-epsilon losses.
constructive: no
opportunity: Euclidean Kakeya has no applied channel. The finite-field Kakeya bounds used in randomness extractors and mergers are a different, already-solved problem (Dvir).
caveats: Very major claim and not formalized.
evidence: keyword grep build TeX (applications mentioned are within harmonic analysis/PDE only)

title: The L log L Fourier-convergence conjecture
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: The ordinary Fourier series of every function in L log L on the circle converges almost everywhere.
constructive: no
opportunity: Signal processing never relies on a.e. convergence of raw partial sums. It uses Fejer/filtered sums, L^2 convergence or finite DFTs, so a.e. convergence for L log L changes nothing.

title: Real ultraflat Littlewood polynomials and unbounded binary merit factors
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: For every large length N there is a +/-1 sequence whose 'spectrum' (the polynomial on the unit circle) has modulus within (1 +/- eps) sqrt(N) everywhere. As a corollary, the best binary merit factor (signal energy over sidelobe energy) tends to infinity, disproving the long-held belief (Turyn; Golay's ~12.3 heuristic) that it stays bounded.
constructive: partial: the proof chains tools that are randomized-algorithmic in principle (Pippenger-Spencer/Alon-Yuster near-perfect hypergraph packing; Lovett-Meka partial colouring for rounding). But the auxiliary torus polynomial, its integer frequency vectors, the prime q, the block count H and the cutoffs are only shown to exist for each delta, and the paper explicitly asserts 'no useful convergence rate or efficient signing algorithm'.
explicit_constants: None. N0(eta) is unspecified. The auxiliary polynomial p_d needs d~8/delta torus variables (energy recursion M_j>=M_{j-1}+(1-M_{j-1})^2/8), and its Fourier support roughly squares at each step, so it is doubly exponential in d. The Lovett-Meka rounding constant C is unspecified. To beat F~12 one needs eta~0.04, hence tiny delta, so N0 is astronomically large.
opportunity: The real applied value is a REDIRECT, not new codes. The belief that the asymptotic optimal binary merit factor is finite is now known to be false. That covers Turyn's conjecture, Golay's 12.32 estimate and extrapolations of exhaustive LABS data (Mertens: F_opt(inf)>9). Surveys, radar/sonar/CDMA sequence-design texts and LABS-as-benchmark papers, including QAOA scaling studies, should stop quoting a finite asymptotic optimum. Nothing changes at lengths anyone uses: exact LABS optima are known only to N~66, search records are F>9 to N~250 and ~7.8 near N~500, and the best explicit long families give 6.34. The proof gives no N at which it beats any of these. A speculative secondary BENCHMARK: the proof's pipeline (a flat real-valued quadratic-phase waveform, then defect-sensitive discrepancy rounding to signs) could be tried as a seed generator for memetic/tabu LABS solvers at N=10^3-10^5, where the bar is only ~6.3-6.5.
targets: LABS benchmark community (Mertens optimal tables; Bošković/Brglez xLastovka; Gallardo et al. memetic-tabu; Dimitrov et al. long-length records)
QAOA-on-LABS quantum-optimization benchmark (Shaydulin et al., JPMorgan/Argonne 2024)
binary radar/sonar/CDMA code-design literature (Golay merit factor; Jedwab-Katz-Schmidt 6.34 families)
BPSK-OFDM PMEPR literature (Rudin-Shapiro / Golay complementary sequences, PMEPR<=2)

Then spend 2-3 days testing relax-and-round (a sampled real quadratic-phase waveform plus Lovett-Meka or Gram-Schmidt-walk rounding) against Legendre-rotation seeds at N=10^3-10^4.

title: Fourier restriction for positively curved surfaces
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: The Fourier extension operator for any compact positively curved surface in R^3 is bounded L^p -> L^p for all p>3. This is the 3D restriction conjecture in its diagonal form.
constructive: no
opportunity: Restriction estimates feed dispersive-PDE well-posedness theory (Strichartz-type bounds). They do not feed numerical solvers, imaging or diffraction computations, which work in L^2 or with finite data.
caveats: Major open-problem claim, not formalized.

title: The three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Smoothly tapered spherical Fourier cutoffs (Bochner-Riesz means of order delta) are bounded on L^p(R^3) for the full conjectured range of delta.
constructive: no
opportunity: Bochner-Riesz means are literally radial spectral filters, but practical filtering uses L^2 or L^infinity stability, and L^infinity boundedness for delta>(d-1)/2 is classical. The critical L^p range settled here is not used by any numerical or imaging method.
caveats: Major claim, not formalized.

title: Local smoothing in three dimensions
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Solutions of the 3D wave equation, averaged over a time interval, gain (almost) the conjectured amount of smoothness in L^p for every 2<p<infinity (Sogge's conjecture).
constructive: no
opportunity: Local smoothing is a tool for nonlinear wave PDE theory. It has no counterpart in wave simulation codes or seismic imaging.
caveats: Major claim, not formalized.

title: The exact Sobolev endpoint for Schrödinger convergence
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: The free Schrödinger evolution converges pointwise almost everywhere to its initial data for every initial state in the sharp Sobolev space H^{n/(2(n+1))}.
constructive: no
opportunity: Pointwise convergence as t->0 for rough data is irrelevant to quantum simulation and numerical PDE, which measure errors in L^2/H^s norms.
caveats: Endpoint claim, not formalized.

title: Riesz transforms and rectifiability in higher codimension
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: In R^d, an n-dimensional regular measure whose Riesz transform is L^2-bounded must be uniformly rectifiable (built from Lipschitz pieces) for 2<=n<=d-2.
constructive: no
explicit_constants: bounds depend only on dimension/regularity/operator norm (not explicit)
opportunity: This is geometric measure theory and singular integrals. The only conceivable channel is boundary-integral methods on fractal-like surfaces, and none of them depends on this characterization.

title: Annular variation and dyadic absolute bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: It proves the long-sought L^3 x L^3 -> L^{3/2} bounds for the 'triangular' bilinear Hilbert transform at its symmetric point, including maximal and variational forms.
constructive: no
opportunity: Multilinear singular integrals are pure harmonic analysis with no applied consumer. The explicit constant 40 for the dyadic form is a curiosity.

title: Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz directions
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Taking a Hilbert transform along a Lipschitz-varying direction field in the plane is L^2-bounded at short scales. This answers Stein's question at that scale.
constructive: no
opportunity: Directional singular integrals appear in the analysis of directional image filters only heuristically. No algorithm or guarantee changes.

title: The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: For any ratio q, there are large-measure compact subsets of [0,1] that contain no scaled-and-shifted copy of the geometric sequence {q^n}.
constructive: yes (explicit compact sets)
opportunity: This is a question in real analysis and additive combinatorics with no applied channel.

title: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of centered disk averages
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: Applying the centered disk maximal filter to a W^{1,1} function in the plane increases its total gradient (total variation) by at most a constant factor.
constructive: no
opportunity: Maximal/sup-of-averages filters exist in image processing, but nobody relies on an unspecified-constant TV bound for them. The channel is too weak to act on.

title: An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
subject: Real and complex analysis
plain_english: The trilinear Hilbert transform with slopes 1,2,3 is bounded from L^3 x L^3 x L^3 to L^1.
constructive: no
opportunity: This is pure multilinear harmonic analysis (linked to ergodic/additive-combinatorics questions). There is no applied channel.
caveats: Very major open-problem claim, not formalized.

title: The Mahler conjectures, functional inequalities and polar-product symplectic width
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: The product of a convex body's volume and its polar's volume is minimized by cubes and Hanner polytopes (symmetric case) or simplices (general case). Symmetric polar products have Gromov width 4.
constructive: no (inequality); extremizers explicit
opportunity: Geometry-of-numbers transference bounds used in lattice cryptanalysis rely on Banaszczyk's l2 transference, not Mahler constants. Interior-point/Santalo-point uses are theoretical. No applied channel.

title: Sharp projection-body inequalities and a counterexample to simplex maximization
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Among convex bodies of fixed volume, ellipsoids uniquely minimize the volume of the projection body (Petty, n>=4). The product of two 10-simplices beats the 20-simplex for the reverse problem.
constructive: yes for the counterexample (explicit ratio 22355476/22020096)
opportunity: Projection bodies connect to shadow/X-ray tomography only in the abstract. No reconstruction method uses these affine isoperimetric inequalities.

title: Bounded-distortion L1 embeddings of planar and bounded-treewidth graphs
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Shortest-path distances in any planar graph (or any graph of bounded treewidth) can be written as a positive combination of cut metrics, distorting each distance by at most a constant factor. Equivalently, in such networks the minimum sparsest-cut ratio is within a constant factor of the maximum concurrent multicommodity flow.
constructive: partial: the planar proof is an explicit randomized multiscale cut process on finite grids that could in principle be sampled, but no algorithm or running time is claimed. The treewidth constant comes from an ultrafilter/compactness argument and is non-explicit.
explicit_constants: Planar: fixed parameters R=1e-8, eps=1e-24, a1<=1e-33, kappa_A=a1/1e6, success probability p=2^-(2M_pack+10), separation b below all these. The resulting distortion is ~16m/(pb), roughly 1e60 or more. Treewidth: C_k non-explicit ('compactness argument establishes a positive uniform lower factor without an explicit numerical estimate').
opportunity: This settles the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the GNRS conjecture. The multicommodity-flow (metric) LP has O(1) integrality gap for nonuniform sparsest cut on planar and bounded-treewidth graphs. The paper notes that combining with Gupta-Talwar-Witmer / Cohen-Addad-Mömke-Verdugo gives (2+eps)C_k-distortion embeddings in FPT time for bounded treewidth. However, the planar constant is astronomically large and C_k is not computable from the proof. Rao's O(sqrt(log n)) is <5 for any real n, and Cohen-Addad-Gupta-Klein-Li already give a quasi-polynomial (2+eps) planar algorithm, so nothing changes for graph-partitioning practice (METIS/KaHIP/Scotch are heuristic anyway). The value is theoretical: a polynomial-time O(1) planar sparsest-cut rounding is now plausible via the LP, and making the column/chart process algorithmic with sane constants is a research program.
targets: approximation-algorithms community (planar / minor-free nonuniform sparsest cut; GNRS conjecture)
multicommodity flow-cut gap theory (Linial-London-Rabinovich, Aumann-Rabani line)
first_step: Check whether the planar construction (shortest-path-tree column realization, radial-layer charts, randomized interpolation offsets) can be run as a polynomial-time sampler of cuts given the LP metric. Then estimate empirical distortion on grid, Delaunay and road-network planar graphs.
caveats: The distortion constant is galactic or non-explicit. GNRS for general minor-closed families is still open (needs clique-sum closure). The almost-embeddable corollary composes with Lee-Sidiropoulos's stochastic distortion D.
evidence: lean/docs/089.md; lean/OAI/Combinatorics/PlanarL1 (63 files, 0 sorry); lean/OAI/Combinatorics/TreewidthL1 (33 files, 0 sorry)
web: arXiv 2105.15187 (quasi-poly (2+eps) planar sparsest cut; Rao O(sqrt log n) poly-time)

title: Triangular-lattice optimality, long-range Riesz and Coulomb energies, and spherical logarithmic energy
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: In the plane, the hexagonal (triangular) lattice has the lowest energy per particle for every 'completely monotone' pair interaction (Gaussian, inverse-power, screened Coulomb, ...) and for renormalized Coulomb/Riesz energies. This settles the Abrikosov-vortex (Sandier-Serfaty) conjecture and fixes the O(n) term in the optimal log-energy of n points on the sphere.
constructive: yes: explicit radial Schwartz Fourier certificates verified with rigorous interval arithmetic (python-flint scripts and C++ certificate code in verification/). The sphere result is asymptotic.
explicit_constants: Explicit: packing density pi/(2 sqrt 3), Brauchart-Hardin-Saff constant C_BHS = 2log2 + 1/2 log(2/3) + 3 log(sqrt(pi)/Gamma(1/3)). Sphere expansion error is o(n) with no rate.
opportunity: The action is CERTIFY: practice already assumes all of this, and these results upgrade it to theorems with machine-checkable certificates. Point-set designers benchmarking minimum-log-energy sphere configurations (Smale's 7th problem, RBF-FD/quadrature node sets) can quote the proven C_BHS as the asymptotic O(n) target. 2D crystallization papers (colloids, dusty plasmas, Wigner crystals, Gaussian-core and Yukawa models, all completely monotone in r^2) and Ginzburg-Landau/Abrikosov vortex-lattice work can cite a ground-state theorem instead of numerics. The supplied interval-arithmetic certificate pipeline is also a reusable template for Cohn-Elkies-type LP bounds. There is no new algorithm, and nothing changes for 3D or Lennard-Jones systems.
targets: minimum-energy point sets on S^2 (Womersley tables; Hardin-Saff-Sloane; RBF-FD node generation for spherical PDE)
2D Coulomb gas / jellium and Ginzburg-Landau vortex-lattice community (Sandier-Serfaty, Lewin, Petrache)
first_step: Run the shipped verifiers (python-flint 0.9.0 in Universal-optimality.../verification, C++ certificate in Triangular-minimality.../verification). Then add the proven expansion E_log(n)=(1/2-log2)n^2-(n/2)log n+C_BHS n+o(n) as the reference line in a script that scores published sphere configurations.
caveats: Results compare configurations at fixed density at zero temperature. The sphere asymptotics have an o(n) error with unknown rate. Lennard-Jones and other non-completely-monotone potentials are not covered, and the 3D analogue is open. Physicists already believed every statement.
evidence: preprints/Triangular-minimality-for-planar-Coulomb-renormalized-energy-September-23-2026/build/sections/01-introduction.tex (Thm main, Thm torus, Cor BHS; 'not a construction of near-optimal point sets')

title: Logarithmic and L_p Brunn–Minkowski inequalities and the B-conjecture
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: The volume of the 'logarithmic mixture' of two symmetric convex bodies is at least the geometric mean of their volumes. This yields the L_p Brunn-Minkowski inequality for 0<p<1 and the B-conjecture for even log-concave measures.
constructive: no
opportunity: These are convex-geometry inequalities. The B-conjecture concerns Gaussian measure of dilates, with only remote links to concentration in statistics. No applied consumer.

title: The optimal order of convex-body covering density
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Any convex body in R^n can cover space by translates along a single lattice with density at most C n log n, and some symmetric bodies need c n log n. So the worst case is Theta(n log n).
constructive: no (Rogers-Schmidt mean-hole averaging + Eldan-Klartag marginals + binary-correction hierarchy; existence of the lattice only)
opportunity: The vector-quantization/lattice-code channel is empty. Information-theoretic 'good for covering' lattices (Erez-Litsyn-Zamir) only require covering density 2^{o(n)}, and n^{O(1)} factors are invisible there. Practical quantizers use specific small-dimension lattices (E8, Leech, Barnes-Wall, A_n*) whose covering densities are computed directly. Removing a (log log n)^{O(1)} factor in an existential bound changes no code.
evidence: slice abstract of translative lower-bound paper

title: Dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Take a log-concave probability distribution whose one-dimensional projections all have Gaussian-like tails with scale a. It satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with constant C a^2, independent of dimension. This is the functional inequality that makes Langevin-type samplers converge fast in KL divergence.
constructive: no: the proof argues by contradiction through compactness, a Gaussian-channel/information argument and a tensor hierarchy. C is universal but not given.
opportunity: LSI with constant O(a^2) plugs straight into existing sampler analyses: Vempala-Wibisono ULA-in-KL, proximal/In-and-Out samplers, and Langevin bounds without warm-start dependence. That yields mixing guarantees with a dimension-free LSI constant for log-concave targets that are not strongly log-concave but have psi_2 marginals. Examples are uniform measures on psi_2 convex bodies (cube, l_p balls with p>=2) and constrained or flat-prior posteriors with subgaussian tails. Previously only Poincare/KLS-type or n^{1/4}-dependent LSI bounds (Bizeul) were available. Because C is non-explicit, the gain is in complexity statements and theory texts, not in certified step counts in software.
targets: log-concave sampling theory (Chewi, 'Log-Concave Sampling'; Kook-Vempala-Zhang In-and-Out / proximal sampler analyses)
first_step: Write the corollary: KL mixing of ULA/proximal sampler for centered log-concave targets with linear subgaussian parameter a, with no dimension dependence through the LSI constant. Then check which practical targets satisfy uniform psi_2 marginals after rounding (generic polytopes and flux polytopes are typically only psi_1).
caveats: Requires a centered measure and a uniform linear subgaussian parameter. Many practical log-concave targets are psi_1 only, and strongly log-concave targets are already covered by Bakry-Emery. C is non-explicit and the result is not formalized.

title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in L_p
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: For 1<p<infinity with p!=2, any n points in L_p can be mapped into l_p^d with distortion D using d=exp(C (log n)^{gamma(p)}) coordinates, which is less than any power of n. Exact (distortion-1) embeddings need about n^2 coordinates.
constructive: no (convex-separation minimax + Maurey sampling; 'existential and does not assert an efficient embedding algorithm')
explicit_constants: C_{p,D} unspecified; no uniformity as D->1
opportunity: Practitioners who sketch l_p distances use Indyk-style p-stable linear sketches with median/estimator decoding, which already give (1+eps) estimates with O(log n/eps^2) numbers. They do not need the target to be a normed l_p space. A nonconstructive, nonlinear embedding with super-logarithmic dimension and unspecified C therefore changes no sketching or NN-search system. The n^2 lower bound for exact embeddings is a nice negative fact with no consumer.
evidence: preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex (Thm 1.1 lines 75-108, method lines 160-215, dimension bounds Sec. 'Dimension bounds')

title: Hyperbolicity cones without semidefinite lifts
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Some convex cones defined by real-rooted ('hyperbolic') polynomials cannot be written as a projection of any semidefinite-programming feasible set, however many extra variables are allowed. So hyperbolic programming is strictly more expressive than SDP. A companion paper gives an explicit 23-variable, degree-20 cone that is not an SDP in its own coordinates but has an explicit 100x100 SDP lift with 307 auxiliary variables.
constructive: partial: the nonspectrahedral cone p(X,Z,y)=det((det X)Z - Phi_y(adj X)) and its 100x100 lift (finite coefficient rule) are explicit. The no-lift cone is built from a finite-field-certified rank-20 Hankel seed plus choices with N>10*36^2, so its matrix size is r=20N-1 >~ 2.6e5 and its degree is huge.
explicit_constants: explicit polynomial (degree 20, or 16 after dividing by det X, in 23 vars) and explicit lift sizes; the no-lift example is enormous
opportunity: (1) REDIRECT: any plan to compile every hyperbolicity cone to SDP for MOSEK-class solvers (generalized or projected Lax) is impossible in general. That justifies native hyperbolic-barrier solvers such as DDS (Karimi-Tuncel) and custom cones in Hypatia.jl. However, no practically arising hyperbolic cone is shown non-liftable: derivative relaxations and elementary-symmetric cones are known to be liftable. (2) INSTANCES: the explicit 23-variable cone with its explicit 100x100 lift is a ready-made benchmark. Solve the same conic program natively (degree-20 hyperbolic barrier) and via the lift in MOSEK/Clarabel/SCS, and use the cone as a test case for spectrahedral-representability heuristics.
first_step: Implement p and its gradient/Hessian oracle for DDS; generate the 100x100, 307-aux lift from the coefficient rule in the companion's Section 'lift'; compare native vs lifted solve time and accuracy on random linear objectives.
caveats: Niche community. The separating (no-lift) cone exists only at astronomical size, and the explicit small cone is SDP-liftable, so the separation is not visible at practical sizes. The no-lift paper is not formalized; the nonspectrahedral paper is.

title: The Gaussian propeller conjecture in every dimension
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: However you split Gaussian space into pieces, the sum of the squared lengths of the pieces' Gaussian centers of mass is at most 9/(8 pi), achieved by three 120-degree sectors. Combined with the separately claimed Unique Games theorem, this makes the known SDP-rounding factor for a kernel-clustering problem optimal for polynomial-time algorithms.
constructive: yes for the extremizer (explicit propeller); hardness is a reduction
opportunity: This pins the worst-case approximability of Khot-Naor identity-target kernel clustering on centered PSD inputs at (8 pi/9)(1-1/k), matching the SDP rounding guarantee. The message is to stop looking for better polynomial-time worst-case algorithms for this objective. Practitioners use k-means/spectral heuristics and are not bound by worst-case ratios, so the effect stays inside approximation-algorithms theory. The NP-hardness also inherits all risk of family 102's Unique Games proof.
caveats: Hardness depends on 102 (the UGC claim), which is not formalized in this family. The ratio is worst-case only.

title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström bound
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Given any sequence of vectors of length at most 1 in R^d, you can choose a +/- sign for each so that every running sum stays within C sqrt(d), no matter how long the sequence is. Consequently, any zero-sum family can be reordered so that all partial sums stay within C sqrt(d), which is optimal.
constructive: no: the authors say it 'does not supply an online rule or an efficient algorithm'. The proof builds a Gaussian/Ornstein-Uhlenbeck filtered convex body and uses shifted Steiner symmetrization.
explicit_constants: absolute C=2 D_* A_0/sigma (kappa=1/100, delta=1/4 fixed), but A_0, H_0 and c_1 come from unquantified absolute constants, so C is not numerically specified
opportunity: IP proximity (Eisenbrand-Weismantel): EW's DP and proximity use the l_inf Steinitz bound m*Delta, giving (2m Delta+1)^m states. For columns with Euclidean norm <= Delta_2, the new bound puts prefix sums in an l2 ball of radius C sqrt(m) Delta_2, whose integer-point count is ~(C' Delta_2)^m. That is a factor of about m^{m/2} fewer states in the worst case (Delta_2 <= sqrt(m) Delta), and a dimension-free base for sparse-column IPs. The same improvement applies to the colorful Steinitz bound for block-structured IPs (2-stage stochastic, n-fold). Reality check: Jansen-Rohwedder already get (sqrt(m) Delta)^{2m} via Spencer discrepancy, a 2026 preprint gives an optimal Euclidean proximity sqrt(det(AA^T))-1, and the DP radius needs an explicit C. With C unspecified (plausibly >=100), the gain only appears at m where these DPs are already infeasible, and production MIP solvers do not use them. Prefix-discrepancy applications such as online covariate balancing and scheduling need algorithms, which Dutta-Jha-Jiang 2026 provide at O(sqrt(d)+d^{1/4} log^{7/4} N).
targets: Eisenbrand-Weismantel / Jansen-Rohwedder proximity + DP algorithms for IPs with few constraints (research codes)
block-structured IP proximity (Cslovjecsek-Eisenbrand-Pilipczuk-Venzin-Weismantel; Oertel-Paat-Weismantel colorful Steinitz)
online vector balancing / covariate-balancing experimental design (Gram-Schmidt walk design line)
first_step: Extract an explicit numerical C by tracing A_0, H_0, c_1 and C_phi through survival.tex/matrix.tex; then redo the EW proximity count with an l2 ball to see the crossover m against (2m Delta+1)^m and Jansen-Rohwedder.
caveats: It is existential, and C is not explicit. It does not improve the l_inf Steinitz constant (conjectured O(sqrt(d))), which is what EW's analysis directly uses, and l2->l_inf conversion recovers only O(m Delta).

title: Compact counterexamples to bi-Lipschitz dimension reduction
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Hilbert space contains a compact set with low 'intrinsic dimension' (doubling constant <= 76800) that cannot be embedded into any finite-dimensional space with bounded distortion. So low doubling dimension alone does not allow faithful low-dimensional coordinates.
constructive: yes (explicit multiscale strip construction with r_j=1000^-j)
explicit_constants: doubling constant <= 300*16^2 = 76800; no quantitative finite-n distortion lower bound
opportunity: This answers negatively the Gupta-Krauthgamer-Lee question, posed for algorithmic dimension reduction, of whether doubling subsets of l2 embed bi-Lipschitzly into R^k with k and D depending only on the doubling constant. Theory should stop seeking such reductions and keep using snowflakes (Assouad, Naor-Neiman, Gottlieb-Krauthgamer) or algorithms that work with doubling dimension directly (cover trees, navigating nets). Practitioners already do that. By compactness, finite counterexamples exist for each (k,D), but with no size bound, so no data-scale consequence.
caveats: The result is qualitative only, with no n-point quantitative distortion lower bound. Doubling-dimension NN algorithms are unaffected.

title: The sharp exponential scale of edit-distance distortion
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: The best possible distortion when representing edit distance between strings of length <= d as l1 distances is exp(Theta(sqrt(log d log log d))). The known Ostrovsky-Rabani embedding is therefore optimal up to the constant in the exponent.
constructive: yes: the lower-bound witnesses are explicit binary strings (prime-period hierarchical words with markers, plus a delimiter code), and the upper bound is the known constructive Ostrovsky-Rabani embedding
explicit_constants: c, C, d0 absolute but unspecified; witness length d=exp(Theta(k^2 log k)) for distortion exp(Omega(k log k))
opportunity: This closes the l1-embedding route for edit distance (previous lower bound Omega(log d), Krauthgamer-Rabani). The message to theory is to stop trying to beat Ostrovsky-Rabani via l1 embeddings for edit-distance NN search and sketching, and to use other primitives instead: CGK random-walk embeddings for small distances, direct approximation algorithms (cf. family 121), or q-gram/MinHash sketches. DNA similarity tools (BLAST, minimap2, Mash/sourmash) never used l1 embeddings, so they are unaffected. The explicit hard words could in principle stress-test learned edit-distance embeddings (CNN-ED, NeuroSEED), but with unspecified c the distortion forced at realistic d (10^3-10^6, sqrt(log d log log d) ~ 3-6) is unknown and probably tiny.
targets: edit-distance sketching / NN-search theory (Ostrovsky-Rabani, Andoni-Krauthgamer line)
learned sequence-embedding work for DNA similarity (NeuroSEED, CNN-ED) as a stress-test source
caveats: Lower-bound witnesses only bite asymptotically, and the constants in the exponent are unspecified. Nothing changes for practical alignment or k-mer tools.
evidence: preprints/Edit-Distance-in-l1-Matching-Bounds-up-to-Constants-in-the-Exponent-September-27-2026/build/sections/introduction.tex (Thm 1.1, prior bounds, construction sketch: log word length O(k^2 log k))

title: Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: A regular tetrahedron can be covered by finitely many triangular-based cylinders whose total cross-section area is less than half its smallest shadow. This disproves Bang-type half-area bounds.
constructive: yes (explicit perturbed two-cylinder covers; saving (13/6000) eps^2)
opportunity: This is a plank/covering problem in discrete geometry. No covering, sensing or tomography application uses this half-area bound.

title: The sharp simplex conjecture for isotropic constants
subject: Convex and metric geometry
plain_english: Among all convex bodies, simplices have the largest isotropic constant (the slicing problem in its sharp form). Equivalently, every log-concave random vector has entropy h >= m + 1/2 log det Cov, with equality only for (affine images of) products of exponential variables.
constructive: n/a (sharp inequality; extremizers explicit)
explicit_constants: sharp and explicit: h(f) >= m + 1/2 log det Cov(f). The gap to a Gaussian with the same covariance is <= m(1/2 log(2 pi e) - 1) = 0.4189 nats = 0.604 bits per dimension.
opportunity: The sharp entropy bound drops straight into information-theory guarantees that currently use Marsiglietti-Kostina-type constants (my derivation, not stated in the paper). For any log-concave noise vector (dependent coordinates allowed), additive-noise channel capacity exceeds the Gaussian-noise capacity at equal covariance by at most 0.604 bits per dimension, and the bound is sharp. For log-concave sources under MSE, the rate-distortion gap to the Shannon lower bound is <= 0.604 bits per dimension, versus ~1.05 bits from Marsiglietti-Kostina. This is a CERTIFY-type tightening of textbook-level bounds. It is real but low-stakes, since codec and modem designers do not operate on these worst-case gaps.
targets: information-theory community (Marsiglietti-Kostina log-concave entropy bounds; reverse EPI; rate-distortion with non-Gaussian sources)
first_step: Re-derive the capacity and SLB-gap corollaries with the sharp constant and check them against Marsiglietti-Kostina (arXiv 1704.07766) Theorems 3-5. Confirm the vector case needs no extra assumptions.

title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem: uniform bounds for limit cycles
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: A planar polynomial vector field of degree d has at most B(d) limit cycles (isolated periodic orbits), with B(d) depending only on d but not computed. Separately, the classical Lienard oscillator x'' + f(x)x' + x = 0 with damping polynomial of degree <= 4 has at most 2 limit cycles, and 2 is attained.
constructive: no for B(d) ('does not furnish an effective formula'); the quintic Lienard bound is exact
opportunity: The uniform bound is foundational, with no computable B(d). The quintic Lienard result gives one small but genuine modeling rule. In any classical Lienard oscillator (linear restoring force) whose damping polynomial has degree <= 4, there are at most two limit cycles, which means at most one stable cycle surrounding or surrounded by an unstable one. Birhythmicity (two coexisting stable oscillations) therefore requires damping of degree >= 6, as in Kaiser-type modified van der Pol models of enzyme or circadian birhythmicity. Modelers can cite this instead of perturbative arguments, and it is Lean-formalized.
targets: nonlinear-oscillator / birhythmicity modeling (modified van der Pol, Kaiser model)
bifurcation-analysis users (AUTO, MatCont) as documentation of global cycle counts
caveats: The global count applies only to the classical form x'=y-F(x), y'=-x with deg F<=5. The uniform B(d) theorem is an enormous unformalized claim that also disputes Ilyashenko's 1991 argument. Only the Lienard part is formalized.
evidence: preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/build/sections/01-introduction.tex (Thm uniform; 'does not furnish an effective formula for B(d)')

title: Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: There is a smooth volume-preserving map of the 3-torus whose Koopman operator looks exactly like multiplication by the circle coordinate on L^2. One observable's iterates form an orthonormal basis.
constructive: yes (explicit smooth construction)
opportunity: Koopman-operator/DMD practitioners deal with spectra of concrete systems. An exotic constructed example with simple Lebesgue spectrum offers no algorithmic lever.

title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: If a measure-preserving transformation is mixing, then it is automatically mixing of all orders: correlations of any number of sets decouple as the time gaps grow.
constructive: no
opportunity: Rate-free qualitative mixing has no use for MCMC or statistical-physics practice, where explicit rates matter.

title: Positive metric entropy for the standard map
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: For all sufficiently large kick strengths k, the Chirikov standard map is chaotic on a positive-area set (positive Lyapunov exponent and metric entropy), as Sinai conjectured.
constructive: no (proof by contradiction; k0 exists but is not given)
opportunity: Accelerator, plasma and kicked-rotor physicists already know numerically that for large K the chaotic sea fills almost all phase space, with Lyapunov exponent ~log(K/2). A theorem valid for k>=k0 with unspecified k0 changes no design or simulation decision.
caveats: Physics channel is certification of the already-believed; k0 non-explicit.

title: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: A smooth convex billiard table whose phase space near the boundary is fully foliated by invariant curves (caustics) must be an ellipse.
constructive: no
opportunity: Billiard rigidity has distant ties to inverse spectral problems ('hearing the shape' of a domain), but no measurement or design method depends on it.

title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: The fractal dimension of any self-similar measure on the line equals min(1, random-walk entropy / Lyapunov exponent), even with overlaps.
constructive: n/a (formula)
opportunity: Fractal-dimension formulas for IFS measures have no engineering consumer.

title: Classwise permanence for weakly reversible mass-action systems
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: In any chemical reaction network where every reaction can be 'undone' by some chain of reactions (weak reversibility), with mass-action kinetics and any fixed positive rate constants, concentrations never blow up and never approach zero. Within each conservation class, all trajectories eventually enter one common compact region.
constructive: partial: the trapping polytope is built from a finite affine family via an induction/compactness argument. The existence is constructive in form, but the bounds eps_P are not computable from the proof as written.
explicit_constants: eps_P exists, depending on network, rates and class; not explicit
opportunity: This settles the boundedness and persistence conjectures (Feinberg; Anderson) and permanence for weakly reversible mass-action networks. It also gives an independent route to the global-attractor conclusion for complex-balanced systems and to the existence of a positive equilibrium in every class. CRNT tools already test the hypothesis (e.g. Catalyst.jl isweaklyreversible) but report only deficiency-theorem conclusions. They can now attach a rate-independent dynamical certificate: a weakly reversible network has bounded, persistent, permanent dynamics for all positive rate constants, so no species goes extinct and nothing blows up. The same applies to model-checking in systems biology and molecular programming. No new numerics are needed, only a structural check plus a theorem citation.
targets: Catalyst.jl network analysis (isweaklyreversible, deficiency, iscomplexbalanced; CRNT docs page)
systems-biology model curation (BioModels) and molecular-programming compilers (DNA strand-displacement CRN design)
first_step: Draft a PR to Catalyst.jl's 'Chemical Reaction Network Theory' docs (and optionally a helper returning a persistence/permanence certificate when isweaklyreversible holds) citing the boundedness/persistence theorem (Lean-formalized) and the permanence theorem. Check overlap with Craciun's 2015/2026 GAC preprint first.
caveats: Requires mass-action with constant rates (permanence for time-varying rates is not claimed here). The bounds are not explicit. Only the trajectorywise boundedness/persistence paper is Lean-formalized; the classwise permanence paper is not. Practitioners simulate anyway, so the certificate is a documentation-level gain. Craciun's toric-differential-inclusion work may already cover GAC.

title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: Billiards in any triangle with an angle that is an irrational multiple of pi are ergodic and even weakly mixing. A generic trajectory explores everything and decorrelates in the weak sense.
constructive: no
opportunity: This certifies what Casati-Prosen-type numerics already show for polygonal billiards (pseudointegrable transport, quantum chaos studies). It has no rates, so no transport or simulation decision changes.

title: A C^1 counterexample to the entropy conjecture
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: A once-differentiable (noninvertible) self-map of a compact manifold can have zero topological entropy even though its action on homology grows like 2^n. This refutes the C^1 form of Shub's conjecture.
constructive: yes (explicit construction)
opportunity: Topological-entropy lower bounds from homology are not used in applied dynamics or in computational topology of time series.

title: Zero entropy does not guarantee a smooth positive-volume model
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
plain_english: There is a zero-entropy ergodic system that cannot be realized as any smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of a compact manifold.
constructive: yes (construction)
opportunity: This is pure realization theory in ergodic theory.
evidence: lean/docs/152.md (formalized statement is the finite-entropy version)

title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions
subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory

opportunity: This is pure fractal and probability theory. The authors explicitly disclaim any decision algorithm.

plain_english: For mixing systems, multiple ergodic averages (1/N) sum f1(T^n x) f2(T^{2n} x)... converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals.
